क: क 1. क, the first consonant of the alphabet, and the first of the guttural letters, corresponding in sound to क् in keep or किन्ग्. —क-कार, अस्, m. the letter or sound क. —ककार-वर्ग, अस्, m. the guttural consonants collectively.

क 2. क, कस्, का, किम्, interrog. pron. (see किम् and 2. कद्, and cf. the following words in which the interrogative base क appears, कतम, कतर, कति, कथम्, कदा, कर्हि, का, &c.), who? which? what? In its declension क follows the pronoun तद् (Gram. 223) except in nom. acc. sing. neut., where किम् has taken the place of कद् or कत् in classical Sanskrit; but the old form कद् is found in the Veda. The interrogative sentence introduced by क is often terminated by इति (e. g. कस्य स पुत्र इति कथ्-यताम्, let it be said, ‘whose son is he?’), but इति may be omitted and the sentence lose its direct interrogative character (e. g. कस्य स पुत्रो न ज्ञायते, it is not known whose son he is). क with or without अस्, ‘to be,’ may express ‘how is it possible that?’ ‘what power have I, you, they, &c.?’ (e. g. के मम धन्विनो ऽन्ये, what can the other archers do against me? के आवाम् परित्रातुम्, what power have we to rescue you?). क is often connected with a demonstrative pron. (e. g. को ऽयम् आयाति, who comes here?) or with the potential (e. g. को हरिं निन्देत्, who will blame Hari?). क is sometimes repeated (e. g. कः को ऽत्र, who is there? कान् कान्, whom? whom? i. e. which of them? cf. Gram. 53. a), and the repetition is often due to a kind of attrac-tion (e. g. केषां किं शास्त्रम् अध्ययनीयम्, which book is to be read by whom? Gram. 836. a). When किम् is connected with the inst. c. of a noun or with the indecl. participle it may express ‘what is gained by doing so, &c.?’ (e. g. नीरुजः किम् औ-षधैः, what is the use of medicine to the healthy? किं विलम्बेन, what is gained by delay? किम् ब-हुना, what is the use of more words? किम् पौरु-षं हत्वा सुप्तम्, what manliness is there in killing one asleep ?).

क is often followed by the particles इव, उ, नाम, नु, वा, स्विद्, some of which serve merely to gene-ralize the interrogation (e. g. किम् इव एतद्, what can this be? क उ श्रवत्, who can possibly hear? को नाम जानाति, who indeed knows? को न्व् अयम्, who is this? किं नु कार्यम्, what is to be done? को वा देवाद् अन्यः, who possibly other than a god? कस्य स्विद् हृदयं नास्ति, of what person is there no heart ?).

क is occasionally used alone as an indefinite pro-noun, especially in negative sentences (e. g. न कस्य को वल्लभः, no one is a favourite of any one; नान्यो जानाति कः, no one else knows; कथं स घातयति कम्, how does he kill any one? More usually, however, क is only made indefinite when con-nected with the particles च, चन, चिद्, वा, and अपि, in which case क may sometimes be preceded by the relative य (e. g. ये के च, any persons whatsoever; यस्यै कस्यै च देवतायै, to any deity whatso-ever; यानि कानि च मित्राणि, any friends whatsoever; यत् किञ्च, whatever). The particle चन, being composed of च and न, properly gives a negative force to the pronoun (e. g. यस्माद् इन्द्राद् ऋते किञ्चन, without which Indra there is nothing), but the negative sense is generally dropped (e. g. कश्चन, any one; न कश्चन, no one), and a relative is sometimes connected with it (e. g. यत् किञ्चन, anything whatsoever). Examles of चिद् with the interrogative are common; वा and अपि are not so common, but the latter is often found in classical Sanskrit (e. g. कश्चिद्, any one; केचिद्, some; न कश्चिद्, no one; न किञ्चिद् अपि, nothing whatso-ever; यः कश्चिद्, any one whatsoever; केचित् — केचित्, some — others; यस्मिन् कस्मिन् वा देशे, in any country whatsoever; न को ऽपि, no one; न किमपि, nothing whatever).
क may sometimes be used, like 2. कद्, at the beginning of a compound. See क-पूय, &c.

क 3. क, अस्, m. the Who? the Inexplicable, the Unknown. By a forced and erroneous interpreta-tion of the interrogative pronoun occurring in a hymn of the Ṛg-veda (X. 121. कस्मै देवाय हविषा विधेम, what god shall we worship with oblations?) the word क is applied as a name to any chief god or object of worship, as Prajāpati, Brahmā, Viṣṇu; air or wind; the sun; the mind; the soul; Yama; Kāma-deva, the god of love; fire; a peacock; a N. of Dakṣa (a clever or dexterous man?); a knot, joint; the king of the birds; a prince in general; the body; time; wealth, property; sound; light, splendor.

क 4. क, अम्, n. (also regarded as ind.), happiness, joy, pleasure; water; the head, hair; a head of hair. (Perhaps this word has arisen from a far-fetched etymology of the word नाक, ‘pleasure,’ i. e. न-अ-क, ‘not-not-pleasure.’) —क-ज, अस्, आ, अम्, produced in or by water, watery, aquatic; (अम्), n. a lotus. —क-द, अस्, m. ‘giving water,’ a cloud.

क 5. क, a Taddhita affix much used in forming adjectives. It may also be added to nouns to express diminution, deterioration, or similarity (e. g. पुत्रक, a little son; अश्वक, a bad horse or like a horse).
कम्: कम्, ind. See 1. कम्, s. v.

कम् 1. कम्, ind. (Gr. κεν), well, bene (op-posed to अकम्, ‘badly’), a particle placed after the word to which it belongs with an affirmative sense (Well, Yes), which sense, however, is generally so weak that the Indian grammarians are perhaps right in enumerating कम् among the expletives; it is often found attached to a dat. case, giving to the latter a stronger meaning, and is generally placed at the end of the Pāda (e. g. अजीजन ओस्कधीर् भोजनाय कम्, thou didst create the plants for actual food); it is also used as an enclitic with the particles नु, सु, and हि, but is nevertheless treated in the Padapāṭha as a separate word. Rarely कम् seems to be used, like कद् and किम्, as an interrogative particle; some-times it occurs, like किम् and कद्, at the beginning of compounds, marking the strange or unusual cha-racter of anything, [cf. कन्दर्प]: according to native lexicographers कम् means also head; water; food. —कम्-वत्, आन्, अती, अत्, Ved. lovely.

कम् 2. कम्, A. (not used in the con-jugational tenses) चकमे, कमिष्यते, अचकमत, कमितुम्, to wish, desire, long for; to love, be in love with; to have sexual intercourse with: Caus. A. (ep. also P.) कामयते, -ति, काम-याञ्-चक्रे, कामयिष्यते, अचीकमत, कामयि-तुम्, to wish, desire, long for (with pot. or inf., e. g. कामये भुञ्जीत, I wish he may eat; कामये दातुम्, I wish to give); to love, have sexual inter-course with; to be inflamed with love; (with बहु or अत्यर्थम्) to rate or value highly; to cause any one to love, [cf. also कन्]: Desid. चिकमिषते and चिकामयिषते: Intens. चङ्कम्यते; [cf. Lat. comis; also amo with loss of the initial; câ-rus for cam-rus; Hib. caemh, ‘love, desire; fine, hand-some, pleasant;’ caomhach, ‘a friend, a companion;’ caomhaim, ‘I save, spare, protect:’ perhaps Old Germ. scim, scimo, ‘splendor;’ Armen. kamim.]
कंय्य: कंय्य कंय्य, अस्, आ, अम्, or कंय्यु, उस्, उस्, उ (fr. 1. कम्), happy, prosperous; according to other authorities also written कंय or कंयु or कंव।
कंवूल: कंवूल कंवूल or कवूल, अम्, n., N. of the eighth Yoga, = Arabic قبول
कंश: कंश कंश, अस्, अम्, m. n. = कंस, q. v.
कंस्: कंस् कंस्, cl. 2. A. कंस्ते, -सितुम्, to go; to command; to destroy. See कस्।
कंस: कंस कंस, अस्, अम्, m. n. (said to be fr. rt. 2. कम्; according to others fr. the last), a vessel made of metal, a drinking vessel, a cup, a goblet (a noun ending in अस् followed by कंस in a compound does not change its final, e. g. अयस्-कंस, पयस्-कंस, &c.); a particular measure; a metal, tutanag or white copper, brass, bell-metal; cf. कंसास्थि and कांस्य; (अस्), m., N. of a king of Mathurā, son of Ugra-sena and cousin of the Devakī who was mother of Kṛṣṇa, (Ugra-sena being brother of Devaka, who was father of Devakī.) He is usually called the uncle, but was really a cousin of Kṛṣṇa, and became his implacable enemy because it had been prophesied to him that he would be killed by a child of Devakī (Vish. Pur. p. 493); as the foe of the deity he is identified with the Asura Kālanemi; and, as he was ultimately slain by Kṛṣṇa, the latter receives epithets like कंस-जित्, the conqueror of Kaṃsa, &c.; (आ), f. N. of a daughter of Ugra-sena and sister of Kaṃsa. —कंस-कार, अस्, ई, m. f. a worker in pewter or white brass, a bell-founder, considered as an inter-mediate caste. —कंस-जित्, त्, m. an epithet of Kṛṣṇa, the conqueror of Kaṃsa. —कंस-बणिज्, क्, m. a brazier or seller of brass vessels. —कंस-बध, अस्, m. the slaying of Kṛṣṇa; title of a comedy of Śeṣa-Kṛṣṇa. —कंस-माक्षिक, अम्, n. a metallic substance in large grains, a sort of pyrites. —कंस-यज्ञ, अस्, m. a particular sacrifice. —कंस-वती, f., N. of a daughter of Ugra-sena and sister of Kaṃsa and Kaṃsā. —कंस-हन्, आ, m. an epithet of Kṛṣṇa, the destroyer of Kaṃsa. —कंस-हनन, अम्, n. the slaying of Kaṃsa. —कंसाराति (°स-अर्°), इस्, or कंसारि (°स-अरि), इस्, m. epithet of Kṛṣṇa, the enemy of Kaṃsa. —कंसास्थि (°स-अस्°), इ, n. tutanag, white copper, any alloy of tin and copper. —कंसोद्भवा (°स-उद्°), f. a fragrant earth.
कंसक: कंसक, अम्, n. a mineral substance, a salt of iron used as an application to the eyes.
कंसिक: कंसिक, अस्, ई, अम्, made of bell-metal &c.
कंसीय: कंसीय, अस्, आ, अम्, fit for or relating to a cup; (अम्), n. bell-metal.
कंसार: कंसार कं-सार, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. (rice) the grain of which hardens in the centre.
कक्: कक् कक्, cl. 1. A. ककते, चकके, ककि-तुम्, to be unsteady; to be proud; to be thirsty; [cf. Lat. vacillo for qvacillo.]
ककजाकृत: ककजाकृत ककजा-कृत, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. mutilated, torn to pieces.
ककन्द: ककन्द ककन्द, अस्, m. gold; N. of a king.
ककर: ककर ककर, अस्, m., Ved. a kind of bird.
ककर्दु: ककर्दु ककर्दु, उस्, m. (?), Ved. destruction of enemies.
ककाटिका: ककाटिका ककाटिका, f., Ved. a part of the back of the human head, (enumerated together with मस्तिष्क, ललाट, and कपाल।)
ककुञ्जल: ककुञ्जल ककुञ्जल, अस्, m. the bird Cātaka; [cf. कपिञ्जल।]
ककुत्सल: ककुत्सल ककुत्सल, अस्, m., Ved. an ex-pression of endearment applied to a child (?).
ककुद्: ककुद् ककुद्, त्, f. a peak or summit (cul-men); chief, head; any projecting corner; the hump on the shoulders of the Indian bull; a horn; an en-sign or symbol of royalty, as, the white parasol &c.; N. of a daughter of Dakṣa and wife of Dharma. (According to native grammarians ककुद् is the form which must be substituted for ककुद at the end of compounds, e. g. त्रि-ककुद्, three-peaked.) —ककुत्-स्थ, अस्, m., N. of a grandson of Ikṣvāku and son of Śaśāda, said to be so called because in a battle he stood on the hump of Indra, who had been changed into a bull; according to the Rāmāyaṇa he is a son of Bhagīratha. —ककुद्-मत् or ककुन्-मत्, आन्, अती, अत्, running high (as a wave); furnished with a hump; (आन्), m. a mountain; a buffalo with a hump on his shoulders; N. of a medicinal plant; (ती), f. the hip and loins; N. of a metre; [cf. Lat. cacûmen and culmen for caculmen.] —ककुद्मि-कन्या, f. a river (‘mountain-daughter’). —ककुद्-मिन्, ई, इनी, इ, peaked, humped; (मी), m. a mountain; a buffalo with a hump on his shoulders; an epithet of Viṣṇu; N. of a prince of the Ānartas; (इनी), f., N. of a river. —ककुद्रुम, अस्, m. (for ककुद्-द्रुम ?), N. of a jackal in the Pañcatantra. —ककुद्-वत्, आन्, m. a buffalo with a hump on his shoulders; (ती), f., N. of the wife of Pradyumna.
ककुद: ककुद, अस्, अम्, m. n. the summit of a moun-tain; chief, pre-eminent; the hump on the shoulders of the Indian bull; a species of serpent; an ensign or symbol of royalty, as the white parasol, &c. —ककुद-कात्यायन, अस्, m., N. of a Brāhman who was a violent adversary of Śākya-muni. —क-कुदाक्ष (°द-अक्°), अस्, m., N. of a man.
ककुन्दर: ककुन्दर ककुन्दर, अम्, n. the cavities of the loins; (ककुद्मती-दर?; cf. ककुद्मती and कुकुन्दर।)
ककुभ्: ककुभ् ककुभ्, प्, f. (connected with ककुद्), a peak or summit (cacumen); space, region or quarter, as east, west, &c.; N. of a metre of three Pādas con-sisting of eight, twelve, and eight syllables respectively, so called because the second Pāda exceeds the others by four syllables; unornamented hair or the hair hanging down as a tail; a wreath of Campaka flowers; splendor, beauty; a Śāstra or sacred treatise; a Rāgiṇī or personified mode of music; the personi-fied quarter of the sky; a daughter of Dakṣa and wife of Dharma.
ककुभ: ककुभ, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. excelling, distinguished; (अस्), m. a kind of goblin or evil spirit; the tree Terminalia Arjuna; a part of a lute called the belly, a wooden vessel covered with leather placed under its neck to render the sound deeper, or a crooked piece of wood at the end of the lute; one of the Rāgas or personified musical modes; N. of a man; N. of a mountain; (आ), f. space, region, quarter; one of the Rāgiṇīs or female personifications of music. —ककु-भादनी (°भा-अद्°), f. ‘food of the sky,’ a kind of fragrance or perfume; [cf. नली। ]
ककुह: ककुह, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. eminent, excelling others, excellent; (अस्), m., Ved. a part of a carriage, perhaps the seat.
ककेरुक: ककेरुक ककेरुक, अस्, m. a worm in the stomach.
कक्क्: कक्क् कक्क्, a various reading for कख्, q. v.
कक्कट: कक्कट कक्कट, अस्, m., Ved. a species of animal, perhaps a kind of bird.
कक्कुल: कक्कुल कक्कुल, अस्, m., N. of a Bhikṣu.
कक्कोल: कक्कोल कक्कोल, अस्, m., N. of a plant bear-ing a berry, the inner part of which is a waxy and aromatic substance; (अम्), n. or कक्कोलक, अम्, n. a perfume prepared from the berries of this plant.
कक्क्वल्ल: कक्क्वल्ल कक्क्वल्ल, अस्, m. a patronymic of Guṇacandra.
कक्ख्: कक्ख् कक्ख्, a various reading for कख्, q. v.
कक्खट: कक्खट कक्खट, अस्, आ, अम्, hard, solid; (ई), f. chalk. —कक्खट-पत्त्रक, अस्, m. the plant Corchorus Olitorius; (rope is made from its fibre.)
कक्ष: कक्ष कक्ष, अस्, m. (said to be fr. rt. कष्), a lurking or hiding-place; an inner recess, the interior of a forest; a forest of dead trees, a dry wood (the lair of wild beasts), grass, dry grass; a spreading creeper, a climbing plant; the armpit (as the most concealed part of the human body); the side or flank; the orbit of a planet or the circle anciently termed a deferent; sin; a buffalo; a gate; the Beleric Myroba-lan or Terminalia Belerica; (आ), f. painful boils in the armpit, side, shoulder, &c.; an elephant's rope, the string round his neck, also his girth; a woman's girdle or zone; a surrounding wall, a wall; a place surrounded by walls; a court or court-yard; an en-closure; a secluded portion of an edifice; a private or inner chamber, the private apartment for women &c., a room in general; a particular part of a carriage; resemblance, similarity; objection or reply in argu-ment; emulation, rivalry, object of emulation; the jeweller's weight, the Retti; (अस्, आ), m. f. the end of the lower garment which, after the cloth is carried round the body, is brought up behind and tucked into the waistband; a border, lace; the scale or basin of a balance; (अम्), n. a star, a constellation (perhaps a wrong reading for ऋक्ष); (आस्), m. pl., N. of a people. —कक्ष-धर, अम्, n. the part of the body where the upper arm is connected with the shoulder, the shoulder-joint. —कक्ष-प, अस्, m. one of the nine treasures of Kuvera; [cf. कच्छप।] —कक्ष-पुट, अस्, m. the armpit; title of a work on magic. —कक्ष-रुहा, f. a fragrant grass, Cyperus. —कक्ष-शाय, अस्, m. a dog; [cf. कङ्कशाय।] —कक्ष-सेन, अस्, m., N. of a Rā-jarshi. —कक्ष-स्थ, अस्, आ, अम्, situated on the side, seated on the hip or flank. —कक्षाध्याय (°ष-अध्°), अस्, m., N. of a part of a commentary by Bhūdhara on the Sūrya-siddhānta. —कक्षान्-तर (°ष-अन्°), अम्, n. the inner or private apartment. —कक्षा-पट, अस्, m. a cloth passed between the legs to cover the privities. —कक्षा-पुटि, इस्, m., N. of a physician; (wrong reading for काक्षपुटि ?). —कक्षावेक्षक, अस्, m. (कक्षा + अवेक्षक fr. rt. ईक्ष् with अव), a guard of the inner or queen's apartments; keeper of a royal garden; a door-keeper; a poet; a debauchee; a player, a painter; warmth of feeling, strength of sentiment. —कक्षी-कृत, अस्, आ, अम्, assented, pro-mised, (touching the armpit with the hand was per-haps a manner of affirming anything; cf. उरसि कृ under उरस्।) —कक्षोत्था (°ष-उत्°), f. a fragrant grass, Cyperus.
कक्षक: कक्षक, अस्, m., N. of a Nāga.
कक्षतु: कक्षतु, उस्, m., N. of a plant.
कक्षाय: कक्षाय, nom. A. कक्षायते, -यितुम्, to wait for any one in a hidden place, lie in ambush; to intend anything wicked.
कक्षीवत्: कक्षीवत्, आन्, m. (fr. कक्ष्या), N. of a renowned Ṛṣi, sometimes called Pajriya; he is the author of several hymns of the Ṛg-veda, and is described in legends as a son of Uśij and Dīrgha-tamas; (अन्तस्), m. pl. the family or the descendants of Kakṣīvat.
कक्षेयु: कक्षेयु, उस्, m., N. of a son of Raudrāśva and Ghṛtācī.
कक्ष्य: कक्ष्य, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. consisting of shrubs or dry grass; secret; (Sāy.) filling the girth, as a well-fed horse; (आ), f. the girth of an elephant or horse, con-sisting of rope or leather; a woman's girdle or zone; metaphorically the fingers (encircling the Soma cup); an upper garment, the border or lace of one; the enclosure of an edifice, i. e. either the wall &c. so en-closing it, or the court or chamber constituting the enclosure, the inner apartment of a palace; similarity; effort, exertion; a shrub yielding the black and red berry that serves as a jeweller's weight, the Retti or Gunja, Abrus Precatorius; (अम्), n. the cup or re-ceptacle of a balance; a part of a carriage. —कक्ष्य-प्र, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. filling the girth (as a well-fed horse). —कक्ष्या-वत्, आन्, अती, अत्, furnished with a girth. —कक्ष्यावेक्षक, अस्, m. = कक्षा-वेक्षक, q. v. —कक्ष्या-स्तोत्र, अम्, n., N. of a hymn by Divākara-vatsa.
कख्: कख् कख्, cl. 1. P. कखति, -खितुम्, to laugh, laugh at or deride: Caus. P. कखयति, -यितुम्, to cause to laugh; [cf. Lat. cachinnare; Gr. καχάζω, καγχάζω.]
कख्या: कख्या कख्या, f. an enclosure, a division of a large building; (a wrong reading for कक्ष्या।)

कङ्कट: कङ्कट कङ्कट or कङ्कटक, अस्, m. (said to be fr. rt. कङ्क्), mail, defensive armour; an iron hook to goad an elephant.
कङ्कण: कङ्कण कङ्कण, अस्, अम्, m. n. (said to be fr. rt. कै), a bracelet, an ornament of the wrist (used also as a weapon); a string or ribbon tied round the wrist; an ornament round the foot of an elephant; any ornament or trinket; a crest; (ई), f. a small bell or tinkling ornament; an ornament furnished with bells: see किङ्किणी; [cf. Lith. kan-kala-s.] —कङ्कण-पुर, अम्, n., N. of a town, called from कङ्कण-वर्ष. —कङ्कण-प्रिय, अस्, m., N. of a servant of Śiva. —कङ्कण-भू-षण, अस्, आ, अम्, adorned with tinkling orna-ments. —कङ्कण-मणी, f. the jewel in a bracelet. —कङ्कण-वर्ष, अस्, m., N. of an alchemist; epithet of the king Kṣemagupta.

कङ्कणीका: कङ्कणीका, f. an ornament furnished with bells; a string tied round the wrist.

कङ्कतीय: कङ्कतीय, आस्, m. pl., N. of a family.
कङ्कर: कङ्कर कङ्कर, अस्, ई, अम्, vile, bad; (अम्), n. buttermilk mixed with water; a high number, = 100 niyutas.
कङ्करोल: कङ्करोल कङ्करोल, अस्, m. the plant Alan-gium Hexapetalum. See निकोचक।
कङ्कलोड्य: कङ्कलोड्य कङ्कलोड्य, अम्, n. a kind of drug, = अल्कलोड्य।

कङ्कालय: कङ्कालय कङ्कालय or कल्कालय, अस्, m., N. of an author.
कङ्कु: कङ्कु कङ्कु, उस्, m. = कङ्गु, N. of a son of Ugra-sena and brother of Kaṃsa.

कङ्केरु: कङ्केरु कङ्केरु, उस्, m. a kind of crow.
कङ्केल्ल: कङ्केल्ल कङ्केल्ल, अस्, m. the tree Jonesia Aśoka; a kind of pot-herb, Chenopodium Esculentum.
कङ्कोल: कङ्कोल कङ्कोल, अस्, m. a king of the Nāgas; N. of the author of a hymn called Gaṇapatyārādhana.

कङ्गु: कङ्गु कङ्गु, उस्, f. or कङ्गुनी, f. a kind of Panic seed, Panicum Italicum; several varieties of it are cultivated and form articles of food for the poor. —कङ्गुनी-पत्त्रा, f. a kind of grass, = पण्यान्धा।
कङ्गुल: कङ्गुल कङ्गुल, अस्, m. the hand; [cf. अङ्गुलि।]
कच्: कच् कच्, cl. 1. A. कचते, चकचे, कचि-तुम्, to bind; to shine; P. कचति, to sound, cry; [cf. कञ्च्; cf. also Hib. cacht, ‘a strait, a narrow place; bonds, fetters.’]

कचङ्गन: कचङ्गन कचङ्गन, अम्, n. a free market, a place of sale paying no duty or custom; [cf. कराङ्-गण, अङ्गण, and अङ्गन।]
कचङ्गल: कचङ्गल कचङ्गल, अम्, n. the ocean; N. of a region.
कचाकु: कचाकु कचाकु, उस्, उस्, उ, ill-disposed, wicked; intolerable, difficult to be borne; difficult to be attained; (उस्), m. a snake.
कचाटुर: कचाटुर कचाटुर, अस्, m. a gallinule. See दात्यूह।
कचु: कचु कचु, उस्, f. an esculent root, Arum Colocasia and other kinds, many of which are culti-vated for food. See कच्वी।
कचेल: कचेल कचेल, अम्, n. a string or cover con-taining and keeping together the leaves of a manu-script; (perhaps a various reading for काचन।)
कच्चट: कच्चट कच्चट, अम्, n. an aquatic plant, = जलपिप्पली।
कच्चर: कच्चर कच्चर (कद्-चर,) अस्, आ, अम्, dirty, foul; spoiled, spoiled by dirt; vile, wicked, bad; (अम्), n. buttermilk diluted with water; [cf. कङ्-कर, कटुर, &c.]
कच्चिद्: कच्चिद् कच्-चिद् (= कद्-चिद्)। See under 2. कद्।
कच्छ: कच्छ कच्छ, अस्, अम्, m. n. (in the first sense a Prākṛt form for कक्ष; cf. कच्छटिका), the hem or end of a lower garment tucked into the girdle or waistband; (according to some m. f. n. in the next senses, according to others only m.) a bank or any ground bordering on water, as the margin of a river, lake, tank, &c.; a mound or causeway, watery soil, marshy ground, a marsh, a morass, low or flat land skirting mountains; N. of several places; (आस्), m. pl. the people inhabiting them; (अस्), m. a part of a boat; a particular part of a tortoise; a tree, the timber of which is used for making furniture &c., Cedrela Toona or common Tūn; another tree, Hibiscus Populneoides; (आ), f. a cricket; the plant Lycopodium Imbricatum; see वाराही. —कच्छ-देश, अस्, m., N. of a place. —कच्छ-प, अस्, m. a turtle, a tortoise (as inhabiting marshy places); a tumour on the palate; an apparatus used in the distillation of spirituous liquor, a flat kind of still; an attitude in wrestling; the tree Cedrela Toona; one of the nine nidhis or treasures of Kuvera; N. of a Nāga; a son of Viśvā-mitra; N. of a country; (ई), f. a female tortoise or a small species of tortoise; a cutaneous disease, wart or blotch; a kind of lute, also the lute of Sarasvatī (so named from being similar in shape to the tortoise). —कच्छ-प-देश, अस्, m., N. of a place. —कच्छ-भू, ऊस्, f. marshy ground, a swamp, a morass. —कच्छ-रुहा, f. a kind of grass, Dūrva, Agrostis Linearis, Panicus Dactilon. —कच्छ-विहार, अस्, m., N. of a marshy region. —कच्छान्त (°छ-अन्°), अस्, m. the border of a lake or stream. —कच्छेश्वर (°छ-ईश्°), अस्, m., N. of a town.
कच्छटिका: कच्छटिका or कच्छाटिका or कच्छाटी, f. the end or hem of a lower garment or cloth gathered up behind and tucked into the waistband.
कच्छपिका: कच्छपिका, f. a pimple, a blotch or wart; a wart accompanying gonorrhœa.
कच्छर: कच्छर, आस्, m. pl., N. of a people.
कच्छिय: कच्छिय कच्छिय, आस्, m. pl., N. of a people; (various readings have कक्ष and कच्छ।)
कच्छु: कच्छु कच्छु, उस्, or कच्छू, ऊस्, f. (said to be fr. rt. कष्), itch, formation of watery pustules on the hands &c., scab. कच्छुर: कच्छुर, अस्, आ, अम्, scabby, itchy; unchaste, libidinous; (आ), f. the plant Alhagi Maurorum; a species of Curcuma; the plant Carpopogon Pruriens.
कच्छोर: कच्छोर, अम्, n. a kind of Curcuma.
कच्वी: कच्वी कच्वी, f. a plant with an esculent root (Arum Colocasia) cultivated for food.
कज्: कज् कज्, cl. 1. P. कजति, -जितुम्, to be happy; to be confused with joy, pride or sorrow; to grow, (in the last sense a Sautra root.)
कजिङ्ग: कजिङ्ग कजिङ्ग, आस्, m. pl., N. of a people.
कज्जल: कज्जल कज्जल, अस्, m. (in the first sense from कद्-जल), a cloud; (अम्), n. lampblack, con-sidered as a collyrium and applied to the eyelashes or eyelids medicinally or as an ornament, also sulphu-ret of lead or antimony so used; (आ, ई), f. the fish Cyprinus Atratus, or any kind peculiar to stagnant waters, whence the name; (ई), f. sulphuret of mer-cury, Æthiop's mineral; ink. —कज्जल-ध्वज, अस्, m. a lamp. —कज्जल-रोचक, अस्, अम्, m. n. the wooden stand or tripod on which a lamp is placed, a candlestick. —कज्जली-तीर्थ, अम्, n., N. of a Tīrtha.
कज्जलित: कज्जलित, अस्, आ, अम्, covered with lampblack or with a collyrium prepared from it.

कञ्च्: कञ्च् कञ्च्, cl. 1. A. कञ्चते, चकञ्चे, कञ्चितुम्, to bind; to shine; [cf. कच् and काञ्च्।]
कञ्चट: कञ्चट कञ्चट, अस्, m. the aquatic plant Commelina Salicifolia and C. Bengalensis.
कञ्चड: कञ्चड, अस्, m. the plant Commelina Bengalensis.
कञ्चार: कञ्चार कञ्चार, अस्, m. the sun.
कञ्चिका: कञ्चिका कञ्चिका, f. a small boil; the branch of a bamboo.
कञ्चुक: कञ्चुक कञ्चुक, अस्, m. (fr. rt. कञ्च् ?), a dress fitting close to the upper part of the body; armour, mail; a bodice, jacket; the skin of a snake; cloth, clothes; a kind of drawers or short breeches; a strap of leather; the cast-off skin of a snake; (ई), f., N. of a plant.
कञ्चुकित: कञ्चुकित, अस्, आ, अम्, furnished with armour or mail.
कञ्चुकिन्: कञ्चुकिन्, ई, इनी, इ, furnished with armour or mail; (ई), m. an attendant on or overseer of the women's apartments, a chamberlain; a libidinous man, a de-bauchee, one addicted to women; a serpent; N. of several plants, Agallochum, barley, Cicer Arietinum. —कञ्चुकि-रेचक, औ, m. du. the chamberlain and the forester.
कञ्चुलिका: कञ्चुलिका, f. a bodice or jacket.
कञ्चूल: कञ्चूल, अस्, अम्, m. n. an article of female dress, perhaps a bodice.

कञ्जक: कञ्जक कञ्जक, अस्, m. a kind of bird, Gracula Religiosa.

कटन: कटन कटन, अम्, n. roof or thatch of a house.
कटम्ब: कटम्ब कटम्ब, अस्, m. (said to be fr. rt. 2. कट्), a kind of musical instrument; an arrow.
कटम्बरा: कटम्बरा कटम्बरा, f. a medicinal plant. See कटु-रोहिणी।
कटाकु: कटाकु कटाकु, उस्, m. a bird.

कटाटङ्क: कटाटङ्क कटाटङ्क, अस्, m. an epithet of Śiva. See कटङ्कट।
कटार: कटार कटार, अस्, m. a libidinous man, a lecher.
कटाह: कटाह कटाह, अस्, m. (according to the Schol. m. f. n.), a frying-pan, a boiler or a frying-vessel of a semispheroidal shape and with handles; a shallow boiler for oil or butter; a turtle's shell; a well; a winnowing basket; a hill of earth; hell, the infernal regions; a young female buffalo whose horns are just appearing; a dvīpa or division of the known continent, so called, (perhaps the Katai of the Muham-medans or China.)
कटाहक: कटाहक, अम्, n. a pan, a pot.

कटीतल: कटीतल कटीतल, अस्, m. a crooked sword; a sabre or scymitar; [cf. कडितुल।]
कटु: कटु कटु, उस्, उस् or वी, उ (said to be fr. rt. कट्), pungent, acrid, sharp (one of the six kinds of flavour); pungent, stimulating (smell); strong-scented, ill-smelling; bitter, caustic (words); कटेरकग्राम: कटेरकग्राम कटेरक-ग्राम, अस्, m., N. of a village.
कटोदक: कटोदक कटोदक, अम्, n. (fr. कट = कर्त = गर्त ? and उदक), water for a funeral libation, a funeral rite.
कटोरा: कटोरा कटोरा, f. a shallow cup.
कटोल: कटोल कटोल, अस्, m. (said to be fr. rt. कट्), a pungent flavour; a man of an inferior and degraded tribe, a Caṇḍāla, a Pariah, &c.; (अस्, आ, अम्), pungent. —कटोल-वीणा, f. a kind of lute played by the common people or Caṇḍālas.
कट्टार: कट्टार कट्टार, अस्, m. a weapon, a dagger.
कट्वर: कट्वर कट्वर, अस्, आ, अम्, despised; (अम्), n. the skim or whey of curds; buttermilk with water; a sauce, condiment; [cf. कङ्कर, कच्चर, कटुर, कदर, कद्वर।]
कट्वाङ्ग: कट्वाङ्ग कट्वाङ्ग, a wrong reading for खट्वाङ्ग, q. v.

कठर: कठर कठर, अस्, आ, अम्, hard; [cf. कठिन and कठोर।]
कठल्य: कठल्य कठल्य or कठल्ल, अस् or अम्, m. or n. (?), gravel.

कठिनीभूत: कठिनी-भूत, अस्, आ, अम्, hardened, indurated.
कठिल्ल: कठिल्ल कठिल्ल, अस्, m. the plant Momordica Charantia.
कठिल्लक: कठिल्लक, अस्, m. the plant Momordica Charan-tia; Ocymum Sanctum [cf. कठिञ्जर]; Bœrhavia Diffusa.
कठेर: कठेर कठेर, अस्, m. (said to be fr. rt. कठ्), a needy or distressed man, a pauper.

कठोल: कठोल, अस्, आ, अम्, resisting, hard, &c., = कठोर।
कड्: कड् कड्, cl. 1. P. कडति, -डितुम्, to be confused or disturbed by pleasure or pain, to be elated or intoxicated; cl. 6. P. कडति, to con-sume; cl. 10. P. काडयति, -यितुम्, to break off a part, to tear, to separate or detach; to remove the chaff or husk of grain &c.; to preserve; [cf. कण्ड्।]

कडितुल: कडितुल कडितुल, अस्, m. a sword, a scymi-tar, a sacrificial knife; [cf. कटी-तल।]
कड्ड्: कड्ड् कड्ड्, cl. 1. P. कड्डति, -डितुम्, to be hard, rough; to be harsh or severe.
कण्: कण् कण्, cl. 1. P. कणति, चकाण, कणि-ष्यति, अकणीत् or अकाणीत्, कणितुम्, to become small; to sound, cry as in distress; to go or approach: Caus. काणयति, -यितुम्, aor. अचीकणत् and अचकाणत्, to sigh, sound; cl. 10. P. काणयति, यितुम्, to wink; to close the eye with the lids or lashes.

(said to be fr. rt. कण्; according to others related to कना, कनिष्ठ, कनीयस्, कन्या, in all of which the notion of small-ness prevails), a grain, a single seed; a grain or particle of dust; flake (of snow); a drop of water; a spark of fire, the spark or facet of a gem; an ear of corn; an atom, a minute particle; small, minute; (आ), f. a kind of fly, commonly कुमीरापोका; long pepper; cummin seed; (ई), f. a drop, an atom; the plant Premna Spinosa or Longifolia; a kind of corn; see कणिका. —कण-गुग्गुलु, उस्, m., N. of a plant; [cf. गन्धराज, स्वर्णकर्ण, and others.] —कण-जीर, अस्, m. a white kind of cummin seed. —कण-जीरक, अम्, n. small cummin seed. —कण-भक्ष, अस्, m. ‘eating atoms or grains’ (?), i. e. liv-ing on minute particles of food; a nickname of the philosopher Kaṇāda. —कण-भक्षक, अस्, m. a kind of bird; [cf. भारिट, श्यामचतक, शैशिर।] —कण-भक्षण, अम्, n. the eating of grains. —कण-भुज्, क्, m. nickname of Kaṇāda; see कण-भक्ष. —कण-लाभ, अस्, m. a whirlpool. —कण-शस्, ind. in small parts, in minute particles. —कणान्न (°ण-अन्°), अस्, आ, अम्, one whose food consists of grains. —कणान्न-ता, f. the state of one who is made to feed on grains (of rice).

कणिश: कणिश, अस्, अम्, m. n. an ear or spike of corn.
कणिष्ठ: कणिष्ठ, अस्, आ, अम् [cf. कनिष्ठ], the small-est, the most minute.
कणीक: कणीक, अस्, आ, अम्, small, diminutive.
कणीयस्: कणीयस्, आन्, असी, अस्, very small; young, younger; [cf. कनीयस्।]
कणप: कणप कणप, अस्, m. a kind of spear or lance; (various readings have कणय and कनय।)
कणभ: कणभ कणभ, अस्, m. a kind of fly with a sting; [cf. कणा।]
कणाटीन: कणाटीन कणाटीन or कणाटीर or कणाटीरक, अस्, m. a wagtail.

कतम: कतम कतम, अस्, आ, अत् (superlative of 2. क; declined as a pronom., Gram. 236), who or which of many ? (e. g. कतमेन पथा यातास् ते, by which road have they gone?). कतम is often a mere strengthened substitute for क, the superlative affix imparting emphasis. Hence it may occasionally be used for ‘who or which of two?’ (e. g. तयोः कत-मस्मै, to which of these two ?). It may option-ally be compounded with the word to which it refers (e. g. कतमः कठः or कतम-कठः, which Kaṭha out of many?). When followed by च and preceded by यतम an indefinite expression is formed equivalent to ‘any whosoever,’ ‘any whatso-ever,’ &c. (e. g. यतमद् एव कतमच् च विद्यात्, he may know anything whatsoever). In negative sentences कतम with चन or कतम with अपि = not even one, none at all (e. g. न कतमच्-चनाहः, not even on a single day, on no day at all). In addition to the above uses कतम is said to mean ‘best,’ ‘excessively good-looking;’ [cf. 3. क।] —कतमोरग (°म-उर्°), अस्, m., N. of a man.
कतर: कतर, अस्, आ, अत् (comparative of 2. क; declined as a pronom., Gram. 236), who or which of two? whether of two? Analogously to कतम above कतर may occasionally be used to express ‘who or which of many’ (e. g. कतरस्यां दिशि, in which quarter ?), and may optionally be compounded with the word to which it refers (e. g. कतरः कठः or कतर-कठः). In negative sentences कतर with चन = neither of the two (e. g. न कतरश्-चन जिग्ये, neither of the two was conquered; [cf. Gr. πότερος, κότερος; Goth. hvathar; Eng. whether; Lat. uter; Old Germ. huedar; Slav. kotoryi.]
कतरतस्: कतरतस्, ind. on which of the two sides ?
कति: 1. कति (fr. 2. क, declined in pl. only, Gram. 227. अ, all the cases except the nom. voc. and acc. taking terminations, whereas the correlative इति has become fixed as an indeclinable adverb), how many? quot? several (e. g. कति देवाः, how many gods? कति व्यापादयति कति वा ताडयति, some he kills and some he strikes). In the sense of ‘several,’ ‘some,’ कति is generally followed by चिद् or अपि (e. g. कतिचिद् अहानि, for several or some days). कति may be used as an adverb with चिद् in the sense of ‘oftentimes,’ ‘much,’ ‘in many ways’ (e. g. कतिचित् स्तुतः, much or often praised). कति-कृत्वस्, ind. how many times? कति-विध, अस्, आ, अम्, of how many kinds? कति-शस्, how many at a time?
कति 2. कति, इस्, m., N. of a sage, son of Viśvā-mitra and ancestor of Kātyāyana. (For 1. see above.)
कतिथ: कतिथ, अस्, ई, अम्, to what place or stage or degree advanced? (the how-maniest?) with चिद् = advanced to such and such a point (e. g. अहं कतिथश्चिद् आस, I was so far advanced on to such and such a point).
कतिधा: कतिधा, ind. in how many places? in how many parts? how often? कतिधा चित्, everywhere.
कतिपय: कतिपय, अस्, आ or ई, अम् (pl. m. ए and आस्), several, some; a certain number, so many; कति-पयेन अहर्गणेन, after some days; also कति-पयैर् अहोभिः, कतिपयाहस्य, &c. —कतिप-येन or कतिपयात्, ind. with some exertion; [the affix पय has been compared with Gr. ποῖος]
कतिपयथ: कतिपयथ, अस्, ई, अम्, advanced to a certain place or degree.
कतमाल: कतमाल कतमाल, अस्, m. fire; the right form is खतमाल; [cf. also कचमाल and कर-माल।]
कतिक: कतिक or कतिका, f., N. of a town.
कतीमुष: कतीमुष कतीमुष, अम्, n., N. of an Agra-hāra.
कत्ताशब्द: कत्ताशब्द कत्ता-शब्द, अस्, m. the rattling sound of dice.
कत्तृण: कत्तृण कत्-तृण, कत्-तोय, कत्-त्रि। See under 2. कद्।
कत्थ्: कत्थ् कत्थ्, cl. 1. A. कत्थते, -थितुम्, to boast; to mention with praise, to praise or celebrate; to flatter or coax; to abuse, revile.
कत्थन: कत्थन, अस्, आ, अम्, boasting, praising; a boaster, praiser; (अम्), n. boasting.
कत्पय: कत्पय कत्-पय, अस्, आ, अम् (fr. 2. कद् and पय fr. पी = प्यै), Ved. swelling, rising; (Sāy.) one whose waters cause happiness.
कत्र्: कत्र् कत्र्, cl. 10. P. कत्रयति, -यितुम्, to loosen, slacken, remove.
कत्सवर: कत्सवर कत्सवर, अम्, n. the shoulder, the shoulder-blade.
कथ्: कथ् कथ् (this rt. is perhaps connected with कथम्), cl. 10. P., ep. also A. कथयति, -ते, aor. अचकथत् or अचीकथत्, -यि-तुम्, to converse with any one (with inst. c. alone or after सह); to tell, relate, narrate, report, inform, speak about, declare, explain (with acc. of the thing or person spoken about); to describe; to denounce, betray; to suppose, state; Pass. कथ्यते, to be called; be regarded or considered as: Desid. चिक-थयिषति, to desire to tell; [cf. Goth. qvath; Eng. quoth and quote; Gr. κωτίλος, κωτίλλω.]
कथक: कथक, अस्, आ, अम्, a narrator, a relater, one who recites a story or who publicly reads and ex-pounds the Purāṇas &c., one who speaks or tells; (अस्, आ), m. f. the speaker of a prologue or mono-logue; a professional story-teller; chief actor; (अस्), m., N. of a man.
कथन: कथन, अस्, आ, अम्, telling, talkative; (अम्), n. the act of telling, narration, relating, informing.
कथनीय: कथनीय, अस्, आ, अम्, to be said, to be told or declared; worthy of relation, to be named.
कथयान: कथयान, अस्, आ, अम्, telling, speaking.
कथयितव्य: कथयितव्य, अस्, आ, अम्, to be told, to be men-tioned, to be communicated.
कथा: 1. कथा, f. conversation, speech, tale; a fable, a feigned story; talk, mention; (in phil.) disputation; का कथा (with gen. or more commonly with loc. and sometimes with प्रति), what should one say of? how should one speak of? (e. g. एको ऽपि कृच्छ्राद् वर्तेत, भूयसां कथैव का, even one person would live with difficulty, what should one say of many? i. e. how much more many?). —कथाक्रम (°था-आक्°), अस्, m. the commence-ment of a conversation. —कथा-छल, अम्, n. the device of a fable. —कथा-जव, अस्, m., N. of a man. —कथानुराग (°था-अन्°), अस्, m. attention, taking pleasure in a discourse. —कथान्त (°था-अन्°), अस्, m. end of a conversation. —कथान्तर (°था-अन्°), अम्, n. the course of a conversation. —कथा-पीठ, N. of the first Lambaka or book of the Kathā-sarit-sāgara. —कथा-प्रबन्ध, अस्, m. a narrative, a tale, a composed story, a fiction. —क-था-प्रसङ्ग, अस्, m. connection of speeches or discourse, talking, conversation, speaking to or with, rumour, report; (अस्, आ, अम्), talkative, talking much and foolishly, half-witted, foolish; a conjuror, a dealer in antidotes &c. —कथा-प्राण, अस्, m. an actor, the speaker of a prologue or monologue, the intro-ducer of a drama; a professed story-teller. —कथा-मय, अस्, ई, अम्, consisting of tales. —कथा-मुख, अम्, n. the introduction to a tale; N. of the second Lambaka or book of the Kathā-sarit-sāgara. —कथा-योग, अस्, m. conversation, talk, discourse. —कथा-रम्भ (°था-आर्°), अस्, m. beginning of a story or narrative, story-telling. —कथारम्भ-काल (°था-आर्°), अस्, m. story-beginning-time. —कथाराम (°था-आर्°), अस्, m. garden of fable. —कथार्णव (°था-अर्°), अस्, m., N. of a collection of stories at-tributed to Śivadāsa. —कथालाप (°था-आल्°), अस्, m. speech, conversation. —कथावशेष (°था-अव्°), or कथा-शेष, अस्, आ, अम्, one of whom only the narrative remains, i. e. deceased, dead; कथाव-शेषतां गतः, deceased, dead. —कथा-विरक्त, अस्, आ, अम्, reserved, taciturn, disliking conversation. —कथा-सङ्ग्रह, अस्, m. a collection of tales or fables. —कथा-सरित्-सागर, अस्, m. the ocean of the rivers of stories; title of a work of Somadeva. —कथोदय (°था-उद्°), अस्, m. the beginning of a tale, introduction to a tale. —कथोद्घात (°था-उद्°), अस्, m. the opening of a drama by the character that first enters overhearing and repeating the last words of the prelude. —कथोपकथन (°था-उप्°), अम्, n. conversation, conference, narration. —कथो-पाख्यान (°था-उप्°), अम्, n. narration, narrative, relation, telling a story.
2. कथा, ind. (for कथम्), Ved. how? whence? why? Sometimes merely a particle of interrogation (e. g. कथा शृणोति इन्द्रः, does Indra hear? यथा कथा च, in any way whatsoever).
कथानक: कथानक, अम्, n. a small tale; [cf. क्रयाणक, भयानक, &c.]
कथापय: कथापय, nom. P. कथापयति, -यितुम्, to tell, relate, &c.
कथिक: कथिक, अस्, ई, अम्, a narrator, a relater, a story-teller by profession.
कथित: कथित, अस्, आ, अम्, told, said, related; (अम्), n. a conversation, discourse. —कथित-पद, अम्, n. repetition, tautology.
कथीकृ: कथी-कृ, cl. 8. P. A. -करोति, -कुरुते, -कर्तुम्, to transform into a tale. —कथी-कृत, अस्, आ, अम्, transformed into a tale, deceased, dead (e. g. कथी-कृतं वपुः, a body of which one can only give a history, a deceased body).
कथ्य: कथ्य, अस्, आ, अम्, to be spoken about, to be told, fit to be mentioned.
कथ्यमान: कथ्यमान, अस्, आ, अम्, being told or mentioned, under narration.
कथम्: कथम् कथम् (fr. 2. क), ind. how? in what manner? whence? (e. g. कथम् एतत्, how is that? कथम् इदानीम्, how now? what is now to be done? कथम् मारात्मके त्वयि विश्वासः, how can there be reliance on thee of murderous mind? कथम् उत्सृज्य त्वां गच्छेयम्, how can I go away deserting you? कथम् बुद्ध्वा भविष्यति सा, how will she be when she awakes? कथम् मृ-त्युः प्रभवति वेदविदाम्, whence is it that death has power over those that know the Veda? कथम् अवगम्यते, whence is it inferred?). Sometimes कथम् merely introduces an interrogation (e. g. क-थम् आत्मानं निवेदयामि कथं वा आत्मा-पहारं करोमि, shall I declare myself or shall I withdraw ?).

कथम् is often found in connection with the particles इव, नाम, नु, स्विद्, which appear to gene-ralize the interrogation (how possibly? &c.); with नु it sometimes = किमु or कुतस् (e. g. कथं नु, how much more! न कथं नु, how much less!).

कथम् is often connected, like किम्, with the particles चन, चिद्, and अपि, which give an inde-finite sense to the interrogative (e. g. कथं चन, in no way, not at all). When not itself negative कथं चन = in some way, some how; scarcely, with difficulty; न कथं चन, in no way; क-थञ्चित्, some how or other, by some means or other, in any way, with some difficulty, scarcely, in a moderate degree, a little; न कथञ्चित्, not at all, in no way whatever; न कथञ्चिद् न, in no way not, i. e. most decidedly; यथा कथञ्चित्, in any way whatsoever; कथञ्चिद् यदि जीवति, it is with difficulty that he lives; कथम् अपि, some how or other, with some difficulty, scarcely, a little; कथम् अपि न, by no means, not at all. In addition to the above senses lexicographers assert that कथम् may imply ‘amazement, surprise, pleasure, abuse;’ [with कथम् cf. Gr. κατά.] At the beginning of an adjective compound कथम् may have the same sense as किम्. —कथं-रूप, अस्, आ, अम्, of what shape ? —कथं-वीर्य, अस्, आ, अम्, of what power? —कथङ्-कथिक, अस्, आ, अम् (fr. कथम् कथम्), one who is always asking questions, an inquisitive person. —कथङ्-कथिक-ता, f. questioning, inquiring, inquisitiveness. —कथङ्कथित (?), अस्, m. an interrogant, one who puts questions. —कथन्-कर्मन्, आ, आ, अ, how acting. —कथङ्-कारम्, ind. in which manner? —कथन्-ता, f. enquiry, question, demand. —क-थम्-प्रमाण, अस्, आ, अम्, of what measure? —क-थम्-भाव, अस्, m. what state? —कथम्-भूत, अस्, आ, अम्, how being? of what kind?
कद्: कद् 1. कद्, cl. 1. A. कदते, -दितुम्, perf. चकाद, to be confused, suffer mentally; to grieve; to confound; to kill or hurt; to call; to cry or shed tears; चकाद कदनम्, he accomplished a destruction; [cf. Gr. κῆδας; Goth. hatan: cf. also कन्द्।]

कद् 2. कद्, ind. (originally the neuter form of the interrogative pronoun क), Ved. a particle of interrogation, where? कद् is used, like किम्, with the particles चन and चिद् (e. g. न कच्चन उपब्दिः शृण्वे रथस्य, not at any time or in any manner is heard the noise of thy chariot; वेति दिवः-कच्चिद् आ, he comes from heaven now and then). —कच्चिद् is sometimes used, like the simple कद्, as a particle of in-terrogation (e. g. कच्चिद् दृष्टा त्वया दमयन्ती, was Damayantī seen by thee?). कच्चिद् may some-times be equivalent to ‘I hope that’ (e. g. व्याधिर् न कच्चित् ते शरीरम् प्रतिबाधते, I hope no illness afflicts thy body).

कद् at the beginning of a compound marks the uselessness, badness or defectiveness of anything; as in the following examples. —कत्-तृण, अम्, n. a fragrant grass; the plant Pistia Stratiotes. —कत्-तोय, अम्, n. an intoxicating drink, wine or vinous spirit. —कत्-त्रि, अयस्, m. pl. three inferior articles. —कद्-अक्षर, अम्, n. a bad letter, bad writing. —कद्-अग्नि, इस्, m. some or a little fire. —कद्-अध्वन्, आ, m. a bad road. —कद् अन्न, अम्, n. bad food. —कद्-अपत्य, अम्, n. bad posterity; bad children. —कद्-अभ्यास, अस्, m. a bad habit. —कद्-अर्थ, अस्, m. a useless thing; (अस्, आ, अम्), useless, unmeaning; having what purpose or aim? —कदर्थन, अम्, आ, n. f. tormenting, torture. —कदर्थय, nom. P. कदर्थयति, -यि-तुम्, to despise, to estimate lightly; to torment, tor-ture, trouble. —कदर्थित, अस्, आ, अम्, despised, disdained, rejected; rendered useless. —कदर्थी-कृ, cl. 8. P. A. -करोति, -कुरुते, -कर्तुम्, to disdain, despise, to estimate at small value. —क-दर्थी-कृत, अस्, आ, अम्, despised, disdained, ren-dered useless and unavailing. —कद्-अर्य, अस्, आ, अम्, avaricious, miserly; little, insignificant, mean; bad, disagreeable; (अस्), m. a miser. —कदर्य-ता, f. or कदर्य-त्व, अम्, n. avarice; insignificance; badness. —कदर्य-भाव, अस्, m. avarice, stingi-ness. —कद्-अश्व, अस्, m. a bad horse. —कद्-आकार, अस्, आ, अम्, ill-formed, ugly. —कद्-आख्य, अम्, n. the plant Costus Speciosus (‘having a bad name,’ i. e. कुष्ठ or दुष्ट). —कद्-आचार, अस्, आ, अम्, wicked, abandoned, following evil practices; (अस्), m. bad conduct. —कद्-इन्द्रिय, आणि, n. pl. bad organs of sense. —कद्-उष्ट्र, अस्, m. a bad camel. —कद्-उष्ण, अस्, आ, अम्, tepid, lukewarm; (अम्), n. warmth, lukewarmness, gentle warmth; [cf. कवोष्ण, कोष्ण।] —कद्-रथ, अस्, m. a bad carriage. —कद्-वत्, आन्, अती, अत्, containing the word क. —कद्-वद, अस्, आ, अम्, speaking ill or inaccu-rately or indistinctly; contemptible, vile, base. —कल्-लोल, see s. v.
कदन: कदन, अम्, n. destruction, killing, slaughter; war, sin. —कदन-पुर, अम्, n., N. of a town. —क-दन-प्रिय, अस्, आ, अम्, loving slaughter.
कद: कद क-द, अस्, m. a cloud. See 4. क।
कदक: कदक कदक, अस्, m. an awning; [cf. कन्दक।]
कदम्ब: कदम्ब कदम्ब, अस्, m. (said to be fr. 1. कद्), the tree Nauclea Cadamba, a tree with orange-coloured fragrant blossoms; the mustard-seed plant, Sinapis Dichotoma; a kind of grass, Andropogon Serratus; a particular mineral substance; turmeric; (ई), f., N. of a plant; (अम्), n. a multitude, an as-semblage or collection. —कदम्ब-पुष्पा or ई, f. a plant, the flowers of which resemble those of the Kadamba, commonly called Mandīri. —कदम्ब-वायु, उस्, m. a fragrant breeze. —कदम्बानिल (°ब-अन्°), अस्, m. a fragrant breeze, spring.
कदम्बक: कदम्बक, अस्, m. the plant Nauclea Cadamba, Sinapis Dichotoma, = हरिद्रु; (अम्), n. a multitude.
कदम्बद: कदम्बद, अस्, m. the mustard-seed plant, Si-napis Dichotoma.
कदर: कदर कदर, अस्, m. a saw; an iron goad for guiding an elephant; N. of a tree, which may be substituted for Khadira as a sacrificial post; a white sort of Mimosa; (अस्, अम्), m. n. a corn, a callosity of the feet caused by external friction; (अम्), n. coagu-lated milk; [cf. कङ्कर, कच्चर, कटुर, &c.]
कदल: कदल कदल, अस्, ई, m. f. the plantain tree (Musa Sapientum), called also banana. It has a soft perishable stem, poetically a symbol of the frailty of human life; (आ), f., N. of several plants, Pistia Stra-tiotes; Bombax Heptaphyllum; (ई), f. a kind of deer, the hide of which is used as a seat &c.; a flag, a banner, a flag carried by an elephant. —कदली-स्कन्ध, अस्, m. a kind of illusion.
कदलक: कदलक, अस्, m. the plantain or banana tree, Musa Sapientum.
कदलिन्: कदलिन्, ई, m. a kind of antelope.
कदलीक्षता: कदलीक्षता कदलीक्षता, f. a sort of cu-cumber; a fine woman.
कदा: कदा कदा, ind. (fr. 2. क), when? at what time? (with following fut. or pres. tense); how? कदा is sometimes found with a following च and preceding यदा (e. g. यदा कदा च सुनवाम सोमम्, let us press out the Soma as often as may be or at all times); कदा चन, (though originally negative, generally = ) at some time, one day, once; न कदा चन, never at any time; कदा चित्, at some time or other, sometimes, once; न कदा चित्, never; कदापि (कदा-अपि), sometimes, now and then; न कदापि, never; [cf. Gr. κοτέ and ποτέ Lat. quando; Lith. kadà; Slav. kogda.] —कदा-मत्त, अस्, m., N. of a man.
कदूहि: कदूहि कदूहि, इस्, m., N. of a man.
कद्रु: कद्रु कद्रु, उस्, उस् or ऊस्, उ (said to be fr. rt. कव्), tawny, reddish-brown; (उस्), m. tawny (the colour); N. of a Ṛṣi; (ऊस्), f. a Soma vessel (?); a personification described in certain legends which re-late to the bringing down of the Soma from heaven, according to the Brāhmaṇas ‘the earth personified;’ N. of a daughter of Dakṣa, wife of Kaśyapa and mother of the Nāgas or the serpent-race; N. of a plant. —क-द्रु-पुत्र, अस्, m. or कद्रु-सुत, अस्, m. a serpent.
कद्र्यच्: कद्र्यच् कद्र्यच्, आङ्, कद्रीची, अक् (fr. 2. क and rt. अञ्च्), Ved. turned towards what?
कद्वर: कद्वर कद्वर, अम्, n. whey; buttermilk mixed with water; [cf. कङ्कर, कच्चर, कटुर, कट्वर, and कदर।]
कधप्रिय: कधप्रिय कध-प्रिय, अस्, आ, अम्, or कध-प्री, ईस्, ईस्, इ, Ved. friendly towards whom?; (Sāy.) fond of praise.
कन्: कन् कन्, cl. 1. P., Ved. कनति, चकान, अकानीत्, कन्तुम् (of the simple root only the aor. is used), to be satisfied; to be contented with, to accept anything (acc.) with satisfaction; (Sāy.) to love, wish, desire; to shine; to go: Intens. चाकन्ति, impf. चाकन्, perf. चाकन and चके, to be satisfied, to like, enjoy anything (with loc., gen.); to inst.); to be liked, wished, desired (with gen.); to strive after, seek, desire (with acc. or dat.); [cf. कम् and चन्: cf. also Lat. canus, caneo, candeo, can-dela; Hib. canu, ‘full moon.’]
कन: कन कन, a substitute for अल्प, little, small, not occurring alone, but regarded as the source of the following derivatives; [cf. कण।]
कनय: कनय, nom. P. कनयति, -यितुम्, to make less or smaller, diminish.

The popular spelling of the name presents, perhaps, greater variations than that of any place in India (e. g. Kunnoj, Kunnouj, Kinoge, Kinnoge, Kinnauj, Kanoj, Kannauj, Kunowj, Canowj, Canoje, Canauj, &c.). In antiquity this city ranks next to Ayodhyā in Oude. It is known to classical geography as Canogyza; but the name applies also to its dependencies and the surrounding district; the etymology (कन्या, a girl, and कुब्ज, round-shouldered or crooked) refers to a legend relat-ing to the hundred daughters of Kuśanābha, the king of this city, who were all rendered crooked by Vāyu for non-compliance with his licentious desires. कन्याका: कन्याका or कन्यिका, f. a young girl, a virgin.
कन्यस: कन्यस कन्यस, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. कनीयस्), younger; (आ), f. the little finger.
कन्युष: कन्युष कन्युष, अम्, n. the hand below the wrist.
कप्: कप् कप्, a various reading for क्रप्, q. v.
कप: कप कप, आस्, m. pl. a class of demons.
कपट: कपट कपट, अस्, अम्, m. n. (said to be fr. rt. कम्प्), fraud, deceit, cheating, circumvention; (अस्), m., N. of a Dānava; (ई), f. a measure equal to the capacity of the hollows of the two hands joined. —कपट-ता, f. or कपट-त्व, अम्, n. deceitful-ness. —कपट-तापस, अस्, m. one who deceitfully pretends to be an ascetic. —कपट-दैत्य-बध, अस्, m. title of a chapter of the Gaṇeśa-Purāṇa (‘destruction of the Daitya Kapaṭa’). —कपट-प्रबन्ध, अस्, m. fraud, trick, fraudulent plot or contrivance. —कपट-लेख्य, अम्, n. a forged docu-ment, a false or fraudulent statement. —कपट-वचन, अम्, n. deceitful talk. —कपट-वेश, अस्, आ, अम्, assuming a false dress or appearance, masked, disguised; (अस्), m. disguise. —कपटवेशिन्, ई, इनी, इ, disguised, in masquerade. —कपटेश्वरी (°ट-ईश्°), f., N. of a plant.
कपटिक: कपटिक, अस्, ई, अम्, acting deceitfully, fraudu-lent, dishonest, a rogue, a cheat.
कपटिन्: कपटिन्, ई, इनी, इ, fraudulent, dishonest, a cheat; (इनी), f. a kind of perfume, = चीदा।
कपना: कपना कपना, f. (said to be fr. rt. कम्प्), Ved. a worm, a caterpillar; [cf. κάμπη]
कपर्द: कपर्द कपर्द, अस्, m. a small shell or cowrie used as a coin and as a die in gambling, Cypræa Moneta; braided and knotted hair, especially that of Śiva (knotted so as to resemble the cowrie shell).
कपर्दक: कपर्दक, अस्, m. = कपर्द above; (इका), f. Cypræa Moneta. See कपर्द।
कपर्दिन्: कपर्दिन्, ई, इनी, इ, shaggy; wearing braided and knotted hair like the cowrie shell; epithet of Rudra, of Pūṣan, of the descendants of Vasiṣṭha and of Durgā; (ई), m., N. of Śiva; N. of one of the eleven Rudras. —कपर्दि-कारिका, आस्, f. pl., N. of a work. —कपर्दि-स्वामिन्, ई, m., N. of a scholiast.
कपल: कपल कपल, अम्, n., Ved. a half, a part.
कपाट: कपाट कपाट, अस्, ई, अम्, m. f. n. a door, the leaf or panel of a door. —कपाट-घ्न, अस्, m. one who breaks the door, a house-breaker, a thief. —कपाट-सन्धि, इस्, m. the junction of the leaves of a door; a mode of multiplying in which the multiplicand is placed in a certain manner under the multiplying quantity. —कपाटसन्धिक, अस्, आ, अम्, term used for a kind of bandage; similarly अर्ध-कपाटसन्धिक. —कपाटोद्घाटन (°ट-उद्°), अम्, n. a door-key.
कपाल: कपाल कपाल, अम्, n. (said to be fr. rt. कम्प्), a cup, a jar, a dish, used especially for the Puroḍāśa offering (often at the end of a compound, the first member of which is a numeral, e. g. त्रि-कपाल, ‘consisting of three cups’); the shell of an egg, shell of a tortoise; the cotyla of the leg of a man or animal, any flat bone; a kind of leprosy; (अस्, अम्), m. n. the fragment of a vessel, a pot-sherd; a cover or lid; the skull, the cranium, the skull-bone; either half of a water-jar; multitude, assemblage, collection; a treaty of peace on equal terms, = कपाट?; (अस्), m., N. of an intermediate caste; N. of a man; (अम्, ई), n. f. a beggar's bowl; [cf. Gr. κεφαλή; Lat. caput; Germ. haupt; Goth. haubith, Them. haubida.] —कपाल-नालिका, f. a sort of pin or spindle for winding cotton, thread, &c. —कपाल-पाणि, इस्, इस्, इ, having a pot in hand to receive food (as a beggar). —कपाल-भाती, f. a particular sort of penance, consisting in alternate suppression and emission of the breath. —कपाल-भृत्, त्, m. an epithet of Śiva or Mahā-deva (who wears skulls). —कपालमालिन्, ई, इनी, इ, bearing a garland of skulls; epithet of Śiva. —कपाल-मोचन, अम्, n., N. of a Tīrtha. —कपाल-शिरस् (?), आस्, m., N. of a Muni; (a various reading has कलाप-शिरस्।) —कपाल-सन्धि, इस्, m. a treaty of peace on equal terms (= कपाट-सन्धि?). —कपाल-स्फोट, अस्, m., N. of a Rakṣas (‘splitting the skull’).
कपालिका: कपालिका, f. a potsherd; the tartar of the teeth; [cf. कापालिक।]
कपालिन्: कपालिन्, ई, इनी, इ, furnished with or bearing skulls; (ई, इनी), m. f. a man or woman of low caste, son or daughter of a Brāhman mother and a fisherman father; the follower of a certain Śaiva sect, [cf. कापालिक]; (ई), m. an epithet of Śiva (as wearing skulls); N. of one of the eleven Rudras; N. of a servant of Śiva; (इनी), f. the goddess Durgā as the wife of Śiva-kapālin.
कपि: कपि कपि, इस्, इस्, इ (said to be fr. rt. कम्प्), brown; (इस्), m. an ape or monkey; an elephant; the plant Emblica Officinalis or a species of Karañja; incense, storax or impure benzoin, [cf. कपि-ज, कपि-तैल, &c.]; the sun; an epithet of Viṣṇu or Kṛṣṇa; N. of a Muni, the author of a Vedic verse, son of Uru-kṣaya; (इस् or ई), f. a female ape or monkey; [cf. Gr. κῆπος, κεῖπος; Old Germ. affo; Angl. Sax. apa; Eng. ape.] —कपि-कच्छु, उस् or ऊ, ऊस्, f. the plant Mucuna Pruritus. —कपिकच्छु-फलोपमा (°ल-उप्°), f., N. of a plant. —कपि-कच्छुरा, f. the plant Mucuna Pruritus. —कपि-कन्दुक, अम्, n. the skull, the cranium (‘playing-ball of monkeys’). —कपि-केतन, अस्, m. an epithet of Arjuna, the third son of Pāṇḍu. —कपि-केश, अस्, m. monkey's hair (?) . —कपि-कोलि, इस्, m., N. of a plant. —कपि-चूडा, f. or कपि-चूत, अस्, m. the tree Spondias Magnifera. —कपि-ज, अस्, आ, अम्, born of a monkey; (अस्), m. incense, benzoin. —कपि-तैल, अम्, n. benzoin or storax. —कपि-त्व, अम्, n. the state of an ape, apishness. —कपि-ध्वज, अस्, m. an epithet of Arjuna (having a monkey as his symbol, his ensign or arms). —कपि-नामन्, आ, m. incense. —कपि-पिप्पली, f., N. of two different kinds of plants. —कपि-प्रभा, f. the plant Mucuna Pruritus. —कपि-प्रभु, उस्, m. an epithet of Rāma, general of the monkey-force, with which he invaded Laṅkā. —कपि-प्रिय, अस्, m. the tree Spondias Magnifera and the tree Feronia Elephantum. —कपि-भक्ष, अस्, m. the food of apes; N. of a certain eatable substance. —कपि-रथ, अस्, m. an epithet of Rāma; [cf. कपि-प्रभु।] —कपि-रोम-फला, f. the plant Mucuna Pruritus. —कपि-लोम-फला, f. the plant Mucuna Pruritus. —कपि-लोमा, f. a kind of perfume. —कपि-लोह, अम्, n. brass (monkey-coloured metal). —कपिल्लिका, f. (contracted from कपि-वल्लिका?), a plant which bears a seed resembling pepper, Scin-dapsus Officinalis, = गज-पिप्पली. —कपि-वक्त्र, अस्, m. a N. of Nārada, a saint and philosopher and friend of Kṛṣṇa, having a face like a monkey. —कपि-वन, अस्, m., N. of a man. —कपि-वल्ली, f. the plant Scindapsus Officinalis. —कपि-शाक, अस्, अम्, m. n. a cabbage. —कपि-शीर्ष, अम्, n. the upper part or coping of a wall. —कपि-शीर्षक, अम्, n. vermilion, the red sulphuret of mercury. —कपि-शीर्ष्णी, f. a kind of musical instrument. —कपि-ष्ठल (°पि-स्थ°), अस्, m., N. of a Ṛṣi; (आस्), m. pl. the descendants of this Ṛṣi. —कपि-स्कन्-ध, अस्, m., N. of a Dānava. —कपि-स्थल, अम्, n. a place frequented by monkeys. —कपि-स्वर, अस्, m., N. of a man. —कपी-कच्छु, उस्, f. the plant Mucuna Pruritus; see कपि-कच्छु. —कपीज्य, अस्, m. (कपि-इज्या?), the tree Mimusops Kauki. —क-पीन्द्र (°पि-इन्°), अस्, m. the chief of the monkeys; an epithet of Viṣṇu; of Jāmbavat, the father-in-law of Kṛṣṇa; of Hanumat; of Sugrīva, &c. —कपी-वत्, आन्, m., N. of a sage; one of the seven sages of the fourth Manvantara; (ती), f., N. of a river. —कपीष्ट (°पि-इष्°), अस्, m. the tree Feronia Elephantum. —कप्य्-आख्य, अस्, m. incense.
कपिका: कपिका, f., N. of a plant.
कपित्थ: कपित्थ, अस्, m. (त्थ = स्थ fr. rt. स्था, ‘on which monkeys dwell;’ cf. अश्वत्थ), the elephant or wood apple tree, Feronia Elephantum; a particular position of the hands and fingers; (अम्), n. the fruit of Feronia Elephantum. —कपित्थ-त्वच्, क्, n. the bark of the tree Feronia Elephantum. —कपित्थ-पर्णी and कपित्थानी, f., N. of a plant, = चित्र-पत्त्रिका, &c. —कपित्थास्य (°थ-आस्य), अस्, m. a kind of monkey (having a roundish face, in shape like the wood apple).
कपित्थक: कपित्थक, N. of a place in Avanti.
कपित्थिनी: कपित्थिनी, f. a region abounding in Kapitthas.
कपिल: कपिल, अस्, आ, अम्, ‘monkey-coloured,’ brown, tawny, reddish; (अस्), m. the brown or tawny colour; a (brown) dog; incense; N. of an ancient sage, identified by some with Viṣṇu and considered as the founder of the Sāṅkhya system of philosophy; a son of Vitatha; or a son of Vasu-deva by Narācī; or a son of Kardama by Devahūti; a form of fire; an epi-thet of the sun, considered as king of the Nāgas; N. of a Dānava; N. of a mountain; (आस्), m. pl., N. of a people; (आ), f. a brown cow, a fabulous cow cele-brated in the Purāṇas; N. of two plants, a kind of Śiṃśapā or Śiṃśapā itself; the plant Aloe Perfoliata; a sort of perfume; a kind of brass; the common leech; N. of a daughter of Dakṣa; N. of the female elephant of the south-east, the male being called Puṇḍarīka; N. of a river. —कपिल-देव, अस्, m., N. of the author of a Smṛti. —कपिल-द्युति, इस्, m. a N. of Sūrya or the sun. —कपिल-द्राक्षा, f. a vine with brown or tawny coloured grapes. —क-पिल-द्रुम, अस्, m., N. of a perfume or sweet scented wood (काक्षी). —कपिल-धारा, f. an epithet of the Gaṅgā; N. of a Tīrtha; a holy place, a place of pilgrimage. —कपिल-फला, f. a vine with brown grapes. —कपिल-भद्रा, f., N. of a woman. —क-पिल-मत, अम्, n., N. of a work. —कपिल-रुद्र, अस्, m., N. of a poet. —कपिल-वस्तु, उ, n., N. of the town in which Śākya-muni or Buddha was born. —कपिल-शिंशपा, f. a variety of Śiṃśapā with reddish flowers. —कपिल-संहिता, f. title of an Upa-purāṇa, a dialogue between Kapila and Satyajit. —कपिलाक्षी (°ल-अक्°), f. a kind of deer (‘with brown eyes’); a variety of Śiṃśapā with reddish flowers. —कपिलाञ्जन (°ल-अञ्°), अस्, m. an epithet of Śiva; [cf. कपिशाञ्जन।] —कपिला-तीर्थ, अम्, n., N. of a Tīrtha, (any one bathing there obtains 1000 brown cows.) —कपिलावट (°ल-अव्°), अस्, m., N. of a Tīrtha. —कपिलाश्व (°ल-अश्°), अस्, m. an epithet of the god of Indra; N. of a man, a son of Dhundhumāra. —कपिला-ह्रद, अस्, m., N. of a Tīrtha.
कपिलक: कपिलक, अस्, इका, अम्, reddish; (इका), f., N. of a woman.
कपिलीकृ: कपिली-कृ, cl. 8. P. A. -करोति, -कुरुते, -कर्-तुम्, to colour brown or reddish.
कपिश: कपिश, अस्, आ, अम्, ‘ape-coloured,’ brown, reddish-brown; (अस्), m. brown or reddish colour, a com-pound of black and yellow; incense, storax or coarse benzoin; (आ or ई), f. a spirit, a sort of rum; (आ), f. the mother of the demons called Piśācas; N. of a river. —कपिशाञ्जन (°श-अञ्°), अस्, m. an epithet of Śiva. —कपिशा-पुत्र, अस्, m. a Piśāca, an imp or goblin. —कपिशायन (°श-अय्°), अस्, m. a deity; a sort of spirit or rum. —कपिशावदान (°श-अव्°), N. of a Buddhist work.
कपिशित: कपिशित, अस्, आ, अम्, embrowned, made brown or dusky red.
कपिशीका: कपिशीका, f. a kind of spirituous liquor.
कपीत: कपीत, अस्, m., N. of a tree.
कपीतन: कपीतन, अस्, m., N. of several plants; a tree bearing an acid fruit, Spondias Magnifera; the plant Thespesia Populnea; Acacia Sirisa; the holy fig tree, Ficus Religiosa; the betel nut tree, Areca Faufel; Ægle Marmelos.
कपिजङ्घिका: कपिजङ्घिका कपिजङ्घिका, f. a kind of ant; also spelt कपिजाङ्घिका।
कपिञ्जल: कपिञ्जल कपिञ्जल, अस्, m. (fr. क + पिञ्जल?, sometimes कपिङ्गल), a bird, the francoline par-tridge; the Caṭaka; N. of a man; also of a sparrow; (आ), f., N. of a river. —कपिञ्जलार्म (°ल-अर्°), अम्, n., N. of a region (?) .
कपुच्छल: कपुच्छल क-पुच्छल, अम्, n., Ved. the fore part of a sacrificial ladle, i. e. the part with which the fluid is skimmed off; hair hanging down to the ground, or a lock of hair tied on the right side of the crown of a young Brāhman, when he is invested with the sacerdotal thread.
कपुष्टिका: कपुष्टिका कपुष्टिका, f. a patch of hair on each side of the head; also written कपुष्णिक।
कपूय: कपूय क-पूय, अस्, आ, अम् (see 2. क), smell-ing badly, disgusting, disagreeable.
कपृथ्: कपृथ् क-पृथ्, त्, or क-पृथ, अस्, m. (see 4. क), Ved. ‘causing pleasure,’ membrum virile.
कपोत: कपोत क-पोत, अस्, m. (2. क + पोत, q. v.), a dove, pigeon, especially the spotty-necked pigeon; (in the Vedas often a bird of evil omen); a bird in general; a particular position of the hands; the gray colour of a pigeon; the brightness of antimony (of a gray colour). —कपोत-चरणा, f. a kind of perfume. —कपोत-पाक, आस्, m. pl., N. of a mountain-tribe; (आ), f. a princess of this tribe. —कपोत-पाद, अस्, ई, अम्, having feet like those of a pigeon. —कपोत-पालिका or कपोत-पाली, f. a dove-cot, an aviary or pigeon-house. —कपोत-राज, अस्, m. the king of the pigeons. —कपोत-रेतस, अस्, m., N. of a man. —कपोत-रोमन्, आ, m., N. of a prince. —कपोत-वङ्का, f., N. of a medicinal plant (used as a remedy for the stone). —कपोत-वर्ण, अस्, ई, अम्, of the colour of a pigeon, of a bright gray, lead-gray; (ई), f. small cardamoms. —कपोत-वल्ली, f., N. of a plant. —कपोत-वाणा, f. a kind of perfume. —कपोत-वेगा, f., N. of a plant. —कपोत-सार, अम्, n. the brightness of antimony, antimony. —कपोत-हस्त or कपोत-हस्तक, अस्, m. a mode of joining the hands in prayer, entreaty, or fear, &c. —कपोताङ्घ्रि (°त-अङ्°), इस्, f. a kind of perfume. —कपोताञ्जन (°त-अञ्ज्°), अम्, n. = कापोताञ्जन, the brightness of antimony, antimony. —कपोताभ (°त-आभा), अस्, आ, अम्, of the colour of a pigeon, of a bright gray; (अस्), m. a pale or dirty white colour. —कपोतारि (°त-अरि), इस्, m. a hawk, a falcon.
कपोतक: कपोतक, अस्, m. a small pigeon or dove; a mode of joining the hands; (अम्), n. antimony.
कपोतकीया: कपोतकीया, f. a region abounding in pigeons.
कपोतिन्: कपोतिन्, ई, इनी, इ, having pigeons, pigeon-shaped.
कपोल: कपोल कपोल, अस्, m. (said to be fr. rt. कम्प्), a cheek; (ई), f. the fore part of the knee, the knee-cap or pan; [cf. कपाल।] —कपोल-कवि, इस्, m., N. of a poet. —कपोल-काष, अस्, m. any ob-ject against which the cheeks or temples are rubbed; the elephant's temples and cheeks. —कपोल-फ-लक, अस्, m. the cheek; (perhaps) the cheek-bone. —कपोल-भित्ति, इस्, m. the temples and cheek, the upper part of the face; (perhaps) the opening in the temples of an elephant during rut. —कपोल-राग, अस्, m. colour or flush in the cheek.
कप्फिण: कप्फिण कप्फिण, अस्, m., N. of a man; (various readings have कप्फिल्ल, कफिन, कफिन्, कफिल, कम्फिल्ल।)
कफ: कफ कफ, अस्, m. phlegm, one of the three humors of the body (the other two are वायु and पित्त), watery froth or foam in general. —कफ-कर, अस्, आ or ई, अम्, or कफ-द, अस्, आ, अम्, producing phlegm; occasioning colds. —कफ-कूर्चिका, f. saliva, spittle. —कफ-क्षय, अस्, m. pulmonary consumption. —कफ-घ्न, अस्, ई, अम्, removing phlegm, antiphlegmatic, curing colds (epi-thet of many plants); (ई), f., N. of a plant. —क-फ-ज, अस्, आ, अम्, arising from or produced by phlegm. —कफ-ज्वर, अस्, m. fever arising from excess of phlegm. —कफ-नाशन, अस्, ई, अम्, antiphlegmatic. —कफ-प्राय, अस्, आ, अम्, phlegm-atic. —कफ-वर्धक, अस्, ई, अम्, exciting or increasing phlegm. —कफ-वर्धन, अस्, ई, अम्, exciting or increasing phlegm; (अस्), m., N. of a plant, a species of Tabernæmontana. —कफ-वि-रोधिन्, ई, इनी, इ, obstructing the phlegm; (इ), n. pepper. —कफ-सम्भव, अस्, आ, अम्, arising from phlegm. —कफ-हर, अस्, आ, अम्, or क-फ-हृत्, त्, त्, त्, removing phlegm, antiphlegmatic. —कफात्मक (°फ-आत्°), अस्, आ, अम्, phlegmatic. —कफान्तक (°फ-अन्°), अस्, m. a kind of plant, = वर्वूर. —कफारि (°फ-अरि), इस्, m. dry ginger.
कफल: कफल, अस्, आ, अम्, phlegmatic, having phlegm.
कफिन्: कफिन्, ई, इनी, इ, phlegmatic; filled with mucus; (ई), m. an elephant; a various reading for कप्फिण; (इनी), f., N. of a river.
कफेलू: कफेलू, ऊस्, ऊस्, उ, phlegmatic, causing or exciting phlegm; (ऊस्), m. a plant, Cordia Latifolia.
कफणि: कफणि कफणि, इस्, m. f. the elbow.
कफोणि: कफोणि, इस्, ई, m. f. the elbow. —कफोणि-घात, अस्, m. a stroke with the elbow.
कफौड: कफौड कफौड, अस्, m., Ved. the elbow (?) .
कब्: कब् कब्, cl. 1. A. कबते, -बितुम्, to colour, to tinge with various hues; to praise; [cf. कव्।]
कबन्ध: कबन्ध क-बन्ध or क-वन्ध, अस् or अम्, m. or n. a big barrel or cask, a large-bellied vessel; (metaphorically) a cloud; the belly; the clouds which obscure the sun at sunset and sunrise (some-times they are personified); water; a N. of Rāhu; a headless trunk (shaped like a barrel), especially one retaining vitality; (अस्), m., N. of an Ātharvaṇa and Gandharva; N. of a Muni; N. of the Dānava or Rākṣasa called Danu, who was son of Śrī. (His story is told in Rāmāy. III. 75. It is there related that Indra punished him for his insolence in challenging the god to combat, by striking his head and thighs with his thunderbolt and so pressing them into his body. He had enormously long arms and a huge mouth in his belly. It was predicted that he would not recover his original shape until killed in a battle with Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa. The whole story probably repre-sents one of Indra's battles with the clouds.) —क-बन्ध-ता, f. or कबन्ध-त्व, अम्, n. headlessness, decapitation. —कबन्ध-वध, अस्, m. ‘the slay-ing of Kabandha,’ title of a chapter of the Padma-purāṇa.

कम्ब: कम्ब or कम्भ, अस्, आ, अम्, well (?).

कम्बलीय: कम्बलीय, अस्, आ, अम्, fit for woollen blankets.

2. करक, अस्, आ, अम्, m. f. n. (according to some only m. and f.), hail; a thunderstone (?); (अस्), m. toll, tax, tribute (?). —१। करकासार (°क-आस्°), अस्, m. a shower of hail. —२। करकासार, nom. P. क-रकासारति, to pour or shower down like hail.
करण: करण, अस्, ई, अम्, doing, making, effecting, causing (especially at the end of compounds; cf. अन्त-करण, अन्धङ्-करण, उष्णङ्-करण, &c.); Ved. clever, skilled; (अस्), m., Ved. an assistant; a man of a mixed class, the son of a Śūdra woman by a Vaiśya, or (according to some) of an outcast Kṣa-triya (the occupation of this class is writing, accounts, &c.); a writer, a scribe; (अम्), n. making, doing, producing, effecting, accomplishing (very often as last member of a compound, e. g. मुष्टि-करण, committing theft; विरूप-करण, producing de-formity); an action, especially a religious action; business, occupation (as trade &c.); the special business of any tribe or caste; plastering, spreading anything with the hand; the usage or practice of the writer-caste; an act, a deed; an instrument or means of action, an expedient; an organ, an organ of sense or of speech; (in gram.) the immediate cause of an action, the idea expressed by the instru-mental case, instrumentality; the body; (in law) an instrument, document, a bond; a cause, motive; the posture of an ascetic; posture in sexual intercourse, copulation; pronunciation, articulation; (in gram.) the term used in designating a sound or word when referring to it as an independent part of speech or as separated from its context, (करण may be used in this way, like कार, e. g. इति-करण, the word इति); rhythm, time; dramatic action (?), singing (?); an astrological division of the day, (these Karaṇas are eleven, viz. वव, वालव, कौलव, तैतिल, गर, बणिज, विष्टि, शकुनि, चतुष्पद, किन्तुघ्न, and नाग, two being equal to a lunar day, or the time during which the moon's motion amounts to 6°; the first seven are called अ-ध्रुवाणि or movable, and fill, when eight times repeated, the space from the second half of the first day in the moon's increase to the first half of the fourteenth day in its wane; the four others are ध्रुवाणि or fixed, and occupy the four half-days from the second half of the fourteenth day in the wane of the moon to the first half of the first day in its increase); title of a treatise of Varā-ha-mihira on the motions of the planets; a field; grain (?); the mind or heart (?); (ई), f. a woman of a mixed caste; a surd or irrational number, a surd root in arithmetic. —करण-कुतूहल, अम्, n. title of a work on practical astronomy by Bhāskara. —करण-ग्राम, अस्, m. the senses collectively. —करण-त्राण, अम्, n. the head (‘protecting the organs of sense’). —करण-त्व, अम्, n. instrumentality, medi-ate agency. —करण-नियम, अस्, m. suppression or restraint of the organs of sense. —करण-विन्यय, अस्, m. manner of pronunciation. —करण-सार, अस्, m. title of a work on practical astronomy by Bhāskara. —करण-स्थान-भेद, अस्, m. differ-ence of articulation or organ. —करणाधिकार (°ण-अध्°), अस्, m. a section on articulation.
करणि: करणि, इस्, f. doing, making, effecting (only oc-curring with अ privative, e. g. अ-करणि, q. v.).
करणीय: करणीय, अस्, आ, अम्, to be done or made; feasi-ble, to be accomplished; to be caused or effected.

करहाटक: करहाटक, अस्, m. the tree Vangueria Spinosa; N. of an heretical prince.

(said to be fr. rt. 1. कॄ), the shoot of a bamboo; (अस्), m. a water-jar; a thorny plant, described as growing in deserts and fed upon by camels, Capparisaphylla; (अम्), n. the fruit of this plant; (आ or ई), f. the root of an elephant's tusk; a cricket, a small grasshopper. —करीर-कुण, अस्, m. the fruit season of Cap-parisaphylla. —करीर-प्रस्थ, अस्, m., N. of a town; (a various reading has करीरि-प्रस्थ।)
करीरिका: करीरिका, f. the root of an elephant's tusk.
करीरक: करीरक करीरक, अम्, n. fight, battle.
करीलदेश: करीलदेश करील-देश, अस्, m., N. of a region.
करीष: करीष करीष, अस्, अम्, m. n. (fr. 1. कॄ), rub-bish, refuse, dung; dry cow-dung; N. of a mountain; [cf. आखु-करीष।] —करीष-गन्धि, इस्, m., N. of a man. —करीषङ्-कष, अस्, आ, अम्, sweeping away dung; (आ), f. a strong wind, a gale. —करी-षाग्नि (°ष-अग्°), इस्, m. a fire of dry cow-dung; (this substance is very generally used as fuel in Hindūstan.)
करीषक: करीषक, आस्, m. pl., N. of a people.
करीषिन्: करीषिन्, ई, इणी, इ, abounding in dung; (इणी), f. a region abounding in cow-dung; N. of a river.
करुण: करुण करुण, अस्, आ, अम् (said to be fr. rt. 1. कॄ, but in some of its meanings fr. 1. कृ), mourn-ful, miserable, lamenting; (अम्), ind. mournfully, wofully, pitifully, in distress; (अस्), m. that which causes pity, sorrow, affliction, tenderness, pity, com-passion; one of the nine Rasas or sentiments of a poem, the pathetic sentiment; a fruit tree, the pamplemousse, Citrus Decumana; N. of a Buddha; a Jaina saint; N. of an Asura; (आ), f. pity, com-passion; (ई), f., N. of a plant, also called ग्रीष्म-पुष्पी, चारिणी, &c.; (अम्), n., Ved. an action, a holy work. —करुण-ध्वनि, इस्, m. a cry of distress. —करुण-पुण्डरीक, अम्, n. title of a Buddhist work. —करुण-मल्ली, f. the plant Jasmi-num Sambac; also read करुणा-मल्ली. —करुण-वेदि-त्व, अम्, n. compassion, sympathy. —करुण-वेदिन्, ई, इनी, इ, knowing affliction or distress, sympathising, pitiful. —करुणाकर (°ण-आक्°), अस्, m. the father of Padmanābha. —करुणात्मक (°ण-आत्°), अस्, आ, अम्, compassionate, tender-hearted. —करुणात्मन् (°ण-आत्°), आ, आ, अ, kind. —क-रुणा-पर, अस्, आ, अम्, compassionate, tender. —करुणा-मय, अस्, ई, अम्, gentle, compassionate. —करुणारम्भ (°ण-आर्°), अस्, आ, अम्, engaging in deplorable actions. —करुणार्द्र (°ण-आर्°), अस्, आ, अम्, tender-hearted, soft, sensitive. —करुणार्-धित (°ण-अर्°), अस्, आ, अम्, kind. —करुणा-वत्, आन्, अती, अत्, being in a pitiful state, pitiable. —करुणा-विप्रलम्भ, अस्, m. grief of separation with the un-certainty of meeting again, fears occurring in absence. —करुणा-वृत्ति, इस्, इस्, इ, disposed to pity. —क-रुणा-वेदिता, f. charitableness, kindliness, sympathy.
करुणाय: करुणाय, nom. P. A. -णायति, -ते, -यितुम्, to be in a pitiful condition.
करुणिन्: करुणिन्, ई, इनी, इ, being in a pitiful condition, pitiable.
करुत्थाम: करुत्थाम करुत्थाम, अस्, m., N. of a prince, a son of Dushyanta and father of Ākrīḍa; [cf. अश्वत्थामन्।]
करुन्धक: करुन्धक करुन्धक, अस्, m., N. of a son of Śūra and brother of Vasu-deva.
करुम: करुम करुम, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. an epithet of certain spectral or ghost-like appearances.
करूकर: करूकर करूकर, अम्, n., Ved. the joint of the neck and the chine.
करूळतिन्: करूळतिन् करूऌअतिन्, ई, इनी, इ, Ved. one whose teeth are decayed and broken; [cf. the next.]
करूष: करूष करूष, आस्, m. pl., N. of a people descended from a son of Manu Vaivasvata, (a prince of this people is named Danta-vakra.)
करूषक: करूषक, अस्, m., N. of a son of Manu Vaiva-svata; (अम्), n., N. of a species of fruit.
करेट: करेट करेट, अस्, m. a finger-nail.
करेटव्या: करेटव्या करेटव्या, f. or करेटु, उस्, m. the numidian crane; [cf. करटु, कर्कट, &c.]
करेणु: करेणु करेणु, उस्, m. f. (said to be fr. rt. 1. कृ; cf. 1. कर), a male or female elephant, gene-rally used for the latter; according to some also करेणू; (उस्), m. the tree Pterospermum Aceri-folium; (उस्), f., N. of a plant used as a drug and supposed to grow in Kāśmīra. —करेणु-पाल, अस्, m. the groom or keeper of a female elephant; N. of a man; [cf. कारेणुपालि।] —करेणु-भू, ऊस्, m. an epithet of Pālakāpya. —करेणु-मती, f., N. of the wife of Nakula, daughter of a king of Cedi. —क-रेणु-वर्य, अस्, m. a large or powerful elephant. —करेणु-सुत, अस्, m. an epithet of Pālakāpya.
करेणुक: करेणुक, अम्, n. the poisonous fruit of the plant Kareṇu.
करेणू: करेणू, ऊस्, m. f. a male or female elephant.
करेनर: करेनर करेनर, अस्, m. benzoin or storax. See करेवर।
करेन्दुक: करेन्दुक करेन्दुक, अस्, m. a species of grass, = भू-तृण।
करेवर: करेवर करेवर, अस्, m. benzoin or storax.
करोट: करोट करोट, अस्, m. f. a basin, a cup; the bones of the head, the skull.
करोटक: करोटक, अस्, m., N. of a Nāga.
करोटि: करोटि, इस्, or करोटी, f. a basin, a cup; the skull.
करोत्कर: करोत्कर करोत्कर, करोत्पल, &c. See under 1. and 2. कर।
कर्क्: कर्क् कर्क्, to laugh; a Sautra root, or one occurring in grammatical Sūtras but not in the Dhātu-pāṭha.
कर्क: कर्क कर्क, अस्, आ, अम् (said to be fr. 1. कृ), white; good; excellent; (अस्), m. a white horse; a crab; the sign Cancer; a water-jar; fire; a mirror; N. of various plants, = कर्कट, कर्केतन, and कर्केतिल; beauty; N. of a commentator on Kātyā-yana's Śrauta-sūtras; (ई), f., Ved. a white cow (?). —कर्क-खण्ड, आस्, m. pl., N. of a people. —कर्क-चिर्भिटी (?), f. a small cucumber. —कर्क-फल, अम्, n., N. of a plant. —कर्क-सार, अम्, n. flour or meal mixed with curds. —कर्की-प्रस्थ, अस्, m., N. of a town.
कर्कट: कर्कट, अस्, m. a crab; the sign Cancer; a kind of bird, the numidian crane, Lanius Excubitor; N. of a plant with poisonous tubers, the fibrous root of a lotus; the curved end of the beam of a balance (to which the strings supporting the scale are attached); a kind of coitus; the radius of a circle; compass, circuit; (आ), f. the plant Momordica Mixta; (ई), f. a female crab; a snake (?); a kind of cucumber, Cucumis Utilissimus; the fruit of the plant Bombax Heptaphyllum; the curved end of the beam of a balance &c.; a small water-jar; [cf. कर्कर, कर्-कश; cf. also Gr. καρκῖνος; Lat. cancer.] —कर्कट-पुर, अम्, n., N. of a town. —कर्कट-शृङ्ग, अम्, n. the claw of a crab. —कर्कट-शृङ्गिका or कर्कट-शृङ्गी, f. a plant, the fruit of which is compared to the claw or feelers of a crab, the horn of a goat &c., see अज-शृङ्गी; other names of this plant are काम-नाशिनी, कौलीरा, कुलिङ्गी, &c. —कर्कटाक्ष (°ट-अक्°), अस्, m. the plant Cucu-mis Utilissimus. —कर्कटाख्या (°ट-आख्°), f. the plant Karkaṭa-śriṅgī. —कर्कटाङ्गा (°ट-अङ्°), f. the same plant. —कर्कटास्थि (°ट-अस्°), n. the shell or crust of a crab. —कर्कटाह्व (°ट-आह्°), अस्, m. the plant Ægle Marmelos; (आ), f. the plant Karkaṭa-śṛṅgī. —कर्कटेश (°ट-ईश), अस्, m., N. of a sanctuary.
कर्कटक: कर्कटक, अस्, m. a crab; the sign Cancer; the plant Momordica Mixta (?); a kind of sugar-cane; a hook shaped like the claw of a crab; N. of a Nāga; (ई), f. a female crab; (अम्), n. a poisonous root; a particular fracture of the bones. —कर्कटक-रज्जु, उस्, m. a rope with a hook attached to it, shaped like the claw of a crab. —कर्कटकास्थि (°क-अस्°), n. the shell or crust of a crab.
कर्कटि: कर्कटि, इस्, f. a sort of cucumber, Cucumis Uti-lissimus.
कर्कटिका: कर्कटिका, f., N. of a plant, a kind of gourd; a kernel.
कर्कटिनी: कर्कटिनी, f. the plant Curcuma Xanthorrhiza.
कर्कटु: कर्कटु, उस्, m. the numidian crane; [cf. करटु, &c.]
कर्कन्धु: कर्कन्धु कर्कन्धु, उस्, ऊस्, m. f. (considered by some as an irregular compound of कर्क and अन्धु), the jujube tree, Zizyphus Jujuba; a species of this tree with a larger fruit; (उ), n. the fruit of this tree, or the uneatable fruits of a wild species; (ऊस्), f. the berry of this tree; (उस्), m., N. of a man. —कर्कन्धु-कुण, अम्, n. the fruit season of the Karkandhu tree. —कर्कन्धु-प्रस्थ, अस्, m., N. of a town. —कर्कन्धु-मती, f., N. of a woman (?). —कर्कन्धु-रोहित, अस्, आ, अम्, red like the berries of the jujube tree.
कर्कर: कर्कर कर्कर, अस्, आ, अम्, hard, firm; (अस्), m. a bone; a hammer; a mirror [cf. कर्फर]; a strap of leather (?); N. of a Nāga; (अम्), n. stone, limestone, especially the nodule found in Bengal un-der the name of Kaṅkar; [cf. कर्कट, कर्कश।] —कर्कराक्ष (°र-अक्°), अस्, m. a wagtail. —कर्कराङ्ग (°र-अङ्°), अस्, m. a kind of bird, a gallinule (?). —कर्करान्धुक (°र-अन्°), अस्, m. a blind well, one of which the mouth is overgrown with grass &c. so as to be hidden; also read कर्क-रान्धक; see अन्ध-कूप।
कर्कराटु: कर्कराटु कर्कराटु, उस्, m. a glance, a side-look.
कर्कराटुक: कर्कराटुक कर्कराटुक, अस्, m. the numi-dian crane.
कर्करेटु: कर्करेटु, उस्, m. = the preceding; [cf. करटु, &c.]
कर्कराल: कर्कराल कर्कराल, अस्, अम्, m. n. a curl, a ringlet.
कर्करि: कर्करि कर्करि, इस् or ई, f., Ved. a kind of musical instrument, a lute; (ई), f. a water-jar.
कर्करेट: कर्करेट कर्करेट, अम्, n. the hand curved as a claw for the purpose of grasping anything.
कर्कश: कर्कश कर्कश, अस्, आ, अम्, hard, harsh, rough (opposed to कोमल, श्लक्ष्ण); intangible; violent, cruel; unfeeling, unmerciful; harsh, unkind, miserly; (अस्), m. a sword, a scymitar; N. of several plants, = काम्पिल्ल = गुण्डारोचनी (commonly called Sunda Rochani); a kind of cassia, Cassia or Senna Esculenta; a species of sugar-cane; (आ), f. a thorny plant, Tragia Involucrata; (ई), f. the wild jujube; [cf. कर्कट, कर्कर।] —कर्कश-च्छद, अस्, m. the plants Trophis Aspera and Trichosanthes Diœca; (आ), f. the plant Luffa Acutangula. —कर्कश-त्व, अम्, n. hardness, harshness, rough manners. —कर्-कश-दल, अस्, m. the plant Trichosanthes Diœca; (आ), f. another plant. —कर्कश-वाक्य, अम्, n. harsh or contumelious speech.
कर्कारु: कर्कारु कर्कारु, उस्, उ, m. n. a kind of gourd, Beninkasa Cerifera.
कर्कारुक: कर्कारुक, अस्, m. the plant Convolvulus Pani-culatus.
कर्कि: कर्कि कर्कि, इस्, m. the sign of the zodiac, Cancer; also read कर्किन्, ई, m.
कर्केतन: कर्केतन कर्केतन or कर्केतर, अस्, m. (?) a kind of gem or precious stone.
कर्कोट: कर्कोट कर्कोट, अस्, m. one of the principal serpents or Nāgas of Pātāla; (आस्), m. pl., N. of a people; (अम्), n. a poisonous fruit.
कर्कोटक: कर्कोटक, अस्, m. several plants, Momordica Mixta; Ægle Marmelos; the sugar-cane; N. of a Nāga or serpent; (आस्), m. pl., N. of a barbarous tribe of low origin; (ई), f., N. of a plant; (का), f. the plant Momordica Mixta. —कर्कोटक-विष, अम्, n. the poison of Karkoṭaka.
कर्चूर: कर्चूर कर्चूर, अस्, m., N. of a plant, a kind of Curcuma; (अम्), n. gold; an orpiment; [cf. कर्-बुर and कर्बूर।]
कर्चूरक: कर्चूरक, अस्, m. the plant Curcuma Zerumbet; also read कर्बूरक।
कर्ज्: कर्ज् कर्ज्, cl. 1. P. कर्जति, -जितुम्, to pain or make uneasy.
कर्ण्: कर्ण् कर्ण्, cl. 10. P. कर्णयति, -यितुम्, to pierce, bore. See आ-कर्ण्।
कर्ण: कर्ण कर्ण, अस्, m. (said to be fr. rt. 1. कॄ), the ear, the handle or ear of a vessel; the helm or rudder of a ship; the plants Cassia Fistula and Calo-tropis Gigantea; (in prosody) a spondee, a foot of two long syllables; (in geometry) the hypothenuse of a triangle or the diagonal of a tetragon; N. of a renowned hero in the Mahā-bhārata, king of Aṅga and elder brother by the mother's side of the Pāṇḍu princes, being the son of the god Sūrya by Pṛthā or Kuntī, before her marriage with Pāṇḍu. (Afraid of the censure of her relatives, Kuntī deserted the child and exposed it in the river, where it was found by a charioteer named Adhi-ratha and nurtured by his wife Rādhā; hence कर्ण is sometimes called Sūta-putra or Sūta-ja, sometimes Rādheya, though named by his foster-parents Vasu-ṣeṇa); N. of a son of Viśvajit; (with Buddhists) a son of Mahā-sammata and king in Potāla; N. of a king, father of Viśoka-deva; (अस्, आ, अम्), Ved. eared, furnished with long ears; furnished with chaff (as grain). कर्णे, (in theatrical language) into the ear, in a low voice, aside; अपि कर्णे, Ved. behind the ear or back, from behind, after [cf. अपि-कर्ण]; कर्णं दा, to give ear to, listen to; कर्णम् आ-गम्, to come to one's ears, become known to. —कर्ण-कण्डु, उस् or ऊ, ऊस्, m. f. painful itching of the ear. —कर्ण-कीटा, f. an insect or worm with many feet and of a reddish colour, Julus Cornifex; a small centipede; according to some कर्ण-कीटी. —कर्ण-कुब्ज, अम्, n., N. of an imaginary town. —कर्ण-क्ष्वेड, अस्, m. an affection of the ear, a roaring or constant noise in it. —कर्ण-खरिक, अस्, m., N. of a Vaiśya. —कर्ण-ग, अस्, आ, अम्, touching the ear, hanging on it, next to the ear, extending to the ear. —कर्ण-गूथ, अम्, n. ear-wax; (अस्), m. or कर्ण-गूथक, अस्, m. hardening of the wax of the ear. —कर्ण-गृहीत, अस्, आ, अम्, seized by the ear. —कर्ण-गृह्य, ind. seizing by the ear. —कर्ण-गोचर, अस्, आ, अम्, perceptible to the ear, audible. —कर्ण-ग्राह, अस्, m. a helmsman. —कर्ण-ग्राह-वत्, आन्, अती, अत्, furnished with a helmsman (as a ship). —कर्ण-च्छिद्र, अम्, n. the outer auditory passage;
