कुतस्: कुतस् कुतस्, ind. (fr. 1. कु), from where? whence? from whence? whereto? where? in which direction? wherefore? why? from what cause or motive? because; how? in what manner? in which way? how much less? much less. कुतस् is used sometimes for the abl. case of 2. क = कस्मात् (e. g. कुतः कालात्, since what time?). In अ-कुतस्, which occurs at the beginning of some compounds, कुतस् has an indefinite sense (e. g. अकुतो-मृत्यु, not fearing death from any quarter; cf. अकुतो-भय); कुतस् is also indefinite when connected with the particles अपि, चिद्, and चन (e. g. कुतो ऽपि, from any quarter, from any cause; कुतश्चिद्, from any one, from anywhere; अकुतश्चिद्-भय, not fearing danger from any quarter, not presenting danger on any side; कुतश् चन, (in Ved.) from no side, to no side; यतः कुतश्चिद्, from any person soever). —कुतस्-तराम्, ind. how? in what manner? —कुतो-नि-मित्त, अस्, आ, अम्, having what cause or reason? —कुतो-मूल, अस्, आ, अम्, having what origin?
कुतस्त्य: कुतस्त्य, अस्, आ, अम्, whence come? how hap-pened?
कुतापस: कुतापस कु-तापस, अस्, ई, m. f. (see 1. कु), a wicked ascetic.
कुतित्तिरि: कुतित्तिरि कु-तित्तिरि, इस्, m. (see 1. कु), a species of bird resembling the partridge.
कुतीपाद: कुतीपाद कुतीपाद, अस्, m., N. of one of the Ṛṣis or poets of the Sāma-veda.
कुतीर्थ: कुतीर्थ कु-तीर्थ, अस्, m. (see 1. कु), a bad teacher.
कुतुक: कुतुक कुतुक, अम्, n. eagerness, vehe-mence; desire, inclination; curiosity; [cf. कौतुक and कुतूहल।]
कुतुप: कुतुप कुतुप, अस्, m. a small leathern oil-bottle [cf. कुतू]; (अस्, अम्), m. n. the eighth Mu-hūrta or portion of the day from the last Daṇḍa of the second watch to the first of the third or about noon; an eligible time for the performance of sacri-fices to the manes; [cf. कु-तप।]
कुतू: कुतू, ऊस्, f. a leathern oil-bottle.
कुतूणक: कुतूणक कुतूणक, अस्, m. weakness of the eyes, a disease of the eyes in infants; [cf. कुकू-णक।]
कुतूहल: कुतूहल कुतूहल, अम्, n. (fr. the interroga-tive adv. कुतस् and हल, calling out?), curiosity, interest in any extraordinary matter; desire, in-clination; eagerness, vehemence, impetuosity; what excites curiosity or interest, anything interesting, fun; (अस्, आ, अम्), surprising, wonderful; excellent, best, praised, celebrated; [cf. कौतूहल।] —कुतू-हल-वत्, आन्, अती, अत्, curious, taking an interest in anything.
कुतूहलिन्: कुतूहलिन्, ई, इनी, इ, curious, highly interested in any extraordinary matter, inquisitive; eager, im-patient.
कुतृण: कुतृण कु-तृण, अम्, n. (see 1. कु), an aquatic plant, water house-leek, Pistia Stratiotes.
कुत्थ: कुत्थ कुत्थ, अस् or अम्, m. or n. (?), the fifteenth Yoga (in astronomy).
कुत्र: कुत्र कुत्र, ind. (fr. 1. कु), where? where-to? in which case? when? कुत्र — क्व, where (this) — where (that), i. e. how distant or how dif-ferent is this from that, how little is this consistent with that? कुत्र becomes indefinite when con-nected with the particles अपि, चिद्, चन, e. g. कुत्रापि, anywhere, somewhere, to any place where-soever; कुत्र चिद्, anywhere, somewhere, whereso-ever, wherever, to any place; (sometimes कुत्र चिद् = कस्मिंश्चिद्, e. g. कुत्र चिद् अरण्ये, in a certain wood); न कुत्र चिद्, nowhere, to no place whatsoever; कुत्र चिद् — कुत्र चिद्, in one case — in the other case; sometimes — sometimes; यत्र कुत्र च or यत्र कुत्र चिद्, wherever it be, here or there.

कुन्ति: कुन्ति कुन्ति, अयस्, m. pl., N. of a people; (इस्), m. sing. the prince of this people, also called Kunti-bhoja; कुन्ति is, according to different authori-ties, a son of either Dharmanetra, or of Netra and grandson of Dharma, or of Kratha, or of Vidarbha and father of Dhṛṣṭa, or of Supārśva and grandson of Sampāti and great-grandson of Garuḍa; (ई), f. a N. of Pṛthā, the daughter of a Yādava prince named Śūra, who gave her to his childless cousin Kunti or Kunti-bhoja, by whom she was adopted. She afterwards became one of the two wives of Pāṇḍu. (On one occasion before her marriage she paid such respect to the powerful sage Durvāsas that he taught her an incantation or charm, by virtue of which she was to have a child by any god she liked to invoke. Out of curiosity she invoked the Sun, by whom she had a child, cf. कर्ण; but the Sun afterwards restored to her her maidenhood. Soon after his marriage Pāṇḍu retired to the woods to indulge his passion for hunting. There he killed a male and female deer, who turned out to be a Ṛṣi and his wife in the form of these animals. The sage cursed Pāṇḍu and predicted that he would die in the embrace of one of his wives. Hence Pāṇḍu lived apart from Kunti, but with his approval she made use of her charm and had three sons, Yudhiṣṭhira, Bhīma, and Arjuna, by the three deities Dharma, Vāyu, and Indra respectively; cf. माद्री); N. of a Rākṣasī; the wife of a Brāhman; the plant Bos-wellia Thurifera; a fragrant resin (= गुग्गुलु)। —कुन्ति-नन्दन, अस्, m. a son of Kuntī (the final being sometimes shortened in a comp.), either of the three elder Pāṇḍava princes. —कुन्ति-भोज, अस्, m., N. of a Yādava prince, king of the Kuntis, who adopted Kuntī. —कुन्ती-सुत, अस्, m. a son of Kuntī.

कुप्रिय: कुप्रिय कु-प्रिय, अस्, आ, अम् (see 1. कु), dis-agreeable, contemptible, low, vile, last, worst.
कुप्लव: कुप्लव कु-प्लव, अस्, m. (see 1. कु), a weak or frail raft or float.
कुबधू: कुबधू कु-बधू, ऊस्, f. (see 1. कु), a wicked wife.
कुबन्ध: कुबन्ध कु-बन्ध, अस्, m. (see 1. कु), a dis-graceful stigma; [cf. अङ्क-बन्ध।]
कुबल: कुबल कुबल, कुबल-प्रस्थ, कुबलाश्व, &c. See under कुवल, &c.
कुबुद्धि: कुबुद्धि कु-बुद्धि, इस्, इस्, इ (see 1. कु), a person of base or vile sentiments; stupid, foolish.
कुबेर: कुबेर कुबेर, or in later Sanskrit कुवेर, अस्, m. (said to be fr. rt. कुम्ब् or fr. 1. कु and वेर), originally N. of the chief of the evil beings or spirits of darkness with the epithet Vaiśravaṇa; afterwards the god of riches and treasure, the regent of the northern quarter of the world, which is hence called Kubera-guptā dik; (कुबेर is the son of Viśravas by Iḍaviḍā, the chief of the Yakṣas, and a friend of Rudra; he is represented as having three legs and only eight teeth); with Jainas, the attendant of the nineteenth Arhat of the present Avasarpiṇī; N. of a prince of Deva-rāṣṭra; or N. of the great-grand-father of Vāṇa-bhaṭṭa, the author of the Kādambarī; or of the author of the Dattaka-candrikā; the tree Cedrela Toona; (अस्, आ, अम्), deformed, monstrous; slow, lazy; [cf. कुवेर।] —कुबेर-नलिनी, f., N. of a Tīrtha. —कुबेर-बान्धव, अस्, m. an epithet of Śiva, ‘the relation of Kubera.’ —कुबेर-वन, अम्, n. ‘the forest of Kubera,’ N. of a place. —कुबेर-वल्लभ, अस्, m., N. of a Vaiśya. —कुबेराक्षी (°र-अक्°), f. the plant Bignonia Suaveolens. —कु-बेराचल (°र-अच्°), अस्, m. ‘the mountain of Kubera,’ an epithet of the Kailāsa mountain. —कुबेराद्रि (°र-अद्°), इस्, m. an epithet of the Kailāsa mountain.
कुबेरक: कुबेरक, अस्, m. the tree Cedrela Toona (तुन्न); (इका), f., N. of a woman.
कुबेरिण: कुबेरिण कुबेरिण, अस्, m. (?), N. of a mixed caste.
कुब्ज: कुब्ज कुब्ज, अस्, आ, अम् (fr. 1. कु and rt. उब्ज्?), hump-backed, crooked; (अस्), m. a curved sword, scy-mitar; a sort of fish, Bola Cuja; the plant Achyran-thes Aspera, = अपामार्ग; [cf. न्युब्ज and कन्य-कुब्ज; cf. also Lith. kupra, kupotas; Gr. κυφός, κύπτω Lat. gibbus, gibba, gibber; Germ. Höcker?]. —कुब्ज-कण्टक, अस्, m. a white Mimosa. —कुब्-ज-किरात or कुब्ज-वामन, अम्, n. a hump-backed person and a dwarf. —कुब्जाम्रक (°ज-आम्°), अस् or अम् (?), m. or n. (?), N. of a Tīrtha. —कुब्जा-लीढ (°ज-आल्°), अस्, m., N. of the founder of a sect.
कुब्जक: कुब्जक, अस्, आ, अम्, hump-backed, crooked; (अस्), m. the aquatic plant Trapa Bispinosa; (इका), f. in the word कुब्जिका-तन्त्र, N. of a Tantra; according to some authorities कुब्जिका कुमारी is a girl eight years old personating the goddess Durgā at a festival of this deity.
कुब्जित: कुब्जित, अस्, आ, अम्, crooked, curved, bent.
कुब्र: कुब्र कुब्र, अम्, n. (said to be fr. rt. कुम्ब्), a forest; a hole for sacrificial fire; a ring, an ear-ring; a thread; a cart.
कुब्रह्म: कुब्रह्म कु-ब्रह्म, अस्, m. or कु-ब्रह्मन्, आ, m. (see 1. कु), a degraded or contemptible Brāh-man, one who officiates for Śūdras.
कुभन्यु: कुभन्यु कुभन्यु, उस्, उस्, उ, Ved. desirous of water.
कुभा: कुभा कुभा, f., Ved., N. of a river falling into the Indus, the Kabul river (?); [cf. κωφήν.]
कुभार्य: कुभार्य कु-भार्य, अस्, आ, अम् (see 1. कु), having a bad wife; (आ), f. a bad wife.
कुभुक्त: कुभुक्त कु-भुक्त, अम्, n. (see 1. कु), bad food.
कुभृत्य: कुभृत्य कु-भृत्य, अस्, m. (see 1. कु), a bad servant.
कुमति: कुमति कु-मति, इस्, f. (see 1. कु), vile or base sentiment; slow or weak intellect; folly; (इस्, इस्, इ), or कु-मनीष, अस्, आ, अम्, or कु-मनीषिन्, ई, इणी, इ, of slow intellect, foolish.
कुमन्त्र: कुमन्त्र कु-मन्त्र, अस्, m. bad advice; evil counsel; a charm employed to secure success in a bad enterprise.
कुमन्त्रिन्: कु-मन्त्रिन्, ई, m. a bad counsellor.
कुमार: कुमार कुमार, अस्, m. (fr. कु + मार, fr. rt. मृ ? ‘easily dying;’ by native authorities derived fr. rt. 2. कम्), a child, a new-born child (especially in the earlier language); a boy, a youth, a son; a prince, the heir-apparent associated in the kingdom with the reigning monarch (especially in theatrical language); a groom; a N. of Skanda the god of war, who is also the reputed author of certain grammatical Sūtras (see कलाप); N. of a son of Agni, who is the author of some Vedic hymns; an epithet of Agni; (with Jainas) N. of the attendant of the twelfth Arhat of the present Avasarpiṇī; N. of a Prajāpati; an epithet of Mañju-śrī; a parrot; the tree Capparis Trifoliata [cf. कुमारक]; an epithet of the river Sindhu; (आस्), m. pl., N. of a people; (ई), f. a young girl, one from ten to twelve years old, a maiden; or (in the Tantras) any virgin up to the age of sixteen, or before menstruation has commenced; a daughter; N. of the wife of Bhīma-sena, the son of Parīkṣit; or of a daughter of Vasu-deva by Rohiṇī; an epithet of Sītā, the wife of Rāma; an epithet of the goddess Durgā; the Śyāmā, a bird so named; N. of several plants, Aloe Perfoliata, or the plant Clitoria Ternatea [cf. अपराजिता]; also the plant Jasminum Sambac, and a plant commonly called Bandhyā-karkoṭakī; the blossom of the plants Taruṇī and Modinī; great cardamoms; the most southerly of the nine portions of the known continent, or of Jambu-dvīpa, the southern extremity of the peninsula, whence the modern name Cape Comorin (Kumārī); the central part of the universe, according to Hindū geography, Jambu-dvīpa or India; N. of a river flowing from the mountain Śuktimat; N. of a metre consisting of four lines of sixteen syllables each; (when a name is given to a pupil to indicate his attachment to any particular master, कुमारी may be prefixed to denote that the pupil's object is to gain the affections of the master's daughter, e. g. कुमारी-दाक्ष); (अम्), n. pure gold; [Gr. κόρος, κοῦρος; μεῖραξ, μειράκιον ?]. —कुमार-गुप्त, अस्, m., N. of a prince (‘protected by the god of war’). —कु-मार-घातिन्, ई, m. the slayer of a child. —कुमार-जीव, अस्, m., N. of a plant, = पुत्रञ्जीवक. —कु-मार-त्व, अम्, n. boyhood, youth. —कुमार-दत्त, अस्, m., N. of a son of Nidhipati. —कुमार-दास, अस्, m., N. of a poet. —कुमार-देवी, f., N. of the mother of Samudra-gupta. —कुमार-देष्ण, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. granting perishable gifts; (Sāy.) granting children. —कुमार-धारा, f., N. of a river. —कुमार-पाल, अस्, m., N. of a king, = शालिवाहन (?), also N. of a king of Guzerat (?). —कुमार-भट्ट, अस्, m., N. of a poet. —कु-मार-भृत्या, f. care of a young child, care of a pregnant or lying-in woman, midwifery. —कुमार-ललिता, f. ‘boy's play,’ N. of a metre consisting of four lines of eight syllables each. —कुमार-वन, अम्, n. Kumāra's (i. e. Kārttikeya's) grove. —कुमार-वाहिन्, ई, m. a peacock, (‘carrying the god of war;’ this god being usually represented as borne by a pea-cock.) —कुमार-व्रत, अम्, n. a vow of eternal chastity. —कुमार-सम्भव, अस्, m. ‘the birth of the god of war,’ title of a poem by Kālidāsa. —कु-मार-सू, ऊस्, m. the father of the god of war, an epithet of Agni; (ऊस्), f. the mother of the god of war, an epithet of the river Gaṅgā, also of the god-dess Durgā. —कुमार-सेन, अस्, m., N. of a minister. —कुमार-स्वामिन्, ई, m., N. of the author of a commentary on the Mīmāṃsā-bhāṣya. —कुमार-हारित, अस्, m., N. of a teacher. —कुमाराभिषेक (°र-अभ्°), अस्, m. ‘the inauguration of Kumāra,’ title of the thirteenth book of the Kumāra-sambhava. —कुमारी-तन्त्र, अम्, n., N. of a Tantra. —कु-मारी-पाल, अस्, m. the guardian of a virgin or bride. —कुमारी-पुत्र, अस्, m. the child of an unmarried woman. —कुमारी-पुर, अम्, n. a gynæceum. —कुमारी-पूजा, f. the worship of Kumāri or Durgā, (a ceremony performed at the great Durgā festival, when a girl between ten and twelve years old is placed on a pedestal, as the representative of the goddess, and fed with offerings made to the idol.) —कुमारी-श्वशुर, अस्, m. the father-in-law of a maiden.
कुमारक: कुमारक, अस्, m. a child, a little boy, a boy, a lad, a youth; the pupil of the eye; N. of a Nāga; the plant Capparis Trifoliata; (इका), f. a girl from ten to twelve years old, or generally a virgin; an insect, Sphex Asiatica; double jasmine, Jasminum Sambac; large cardamoms; N. of a part of Bhārata-varṣa, a division of the known continent. —कुमा-रिका-क्षेत्र, अम्, n., N. of a country. —कुमारिका-खण्ड, a section of the Skanda-purāṇa.
कुमारय: कुमारय, nom. P. कुमारयति, -यितुम्, to play, especially as a child.
कुमारयु: कुमारयु, उस्, m. a prince, heir-apparent.
कुमारिक: कुमारिक, अस्, ई, अम्, furnished with girls, abound-ing in them.
कुमारिन्: कुमारिन्, ई, इणी, इ, abounding in girls.
कुमारिल: कुमारिल, अस्, m. or कुमारिल-स्वामिन्, ई, m., N. of a renowned teacher of the Mīmāṃsā philosophy.
कुमारी: कुमारी, ई, ई, m. f. a man or woman desirous of a daughter.
कुमार्ग: कुमार्ग कु-मार्ग, अस्, m. (see 1. कु), a bad way, bad ways, (also used metaphorically.)
कुमालक: कुमालक कुमालक, आस्, m. pl., N. of a people and country, = कुमारक।
कुमालय: कुमालय, nom. P. कुमालयति, -यितुम्, to play, especially as a child; [cf. कुमारय।]
कुमित्र: कुमित्र कु-मित्र, अम्, n. (see 1. कु), a bad friend.
कुमुख: कुमुख कु-मुख, अस्, m. (see 1. कु), a hog.
कुमुद्: कुमुद् कु-मुद्, त्, त्, त् (see 1. कु), unkind, unfriendly; avaricious, niggardly; (त्), n. the plant Nymphæa Esculenta, the esculent white water-lily; the plant Nymphæa Rubra, the red lotus. —कुमुद्-वत्, आन्, अती, अत्, abounding in lotuses; (अती), f. an assemblage of lotuses; a place or pond filled with them; the flexible stalk of a water-lily; N. of a plant bearing a poisonous fruit, Villarsia (Menyanthes) Indica; N. of a sister of the serpent-king Kumuda and wife of Kuśa; N. of the wife of Vimarṣaṇa; N. of a river. —कुमुद्वतीश (°ती-ईश), अस्, m. an epithet of the moon; [cf. कुमुद-बन्धु and the following.]
कुमुद: कु-मुद, अस्, अम्, m. n. the esculent white water-lily, Nymphæa Esculenta (‘exciting what joy!’); red lotus, Nymphæa Rubra; (अम्), n. silver; (अस्), m. camphor; N. of a Nāga; N. of the elephant of the south-west or southern quarter; N. of a Daitya; N. of an attendant of Viṣṇu; N. of a son of Gada by Vṛhatī; N. of a confidant of king Unmattāvanti; one of the monkey-heroes of the Rāmāyaṇa; N. of a poet; N. of a mountain; N. of one of the smaller Dvīpas; (आ), f. several plants, Gmelina Arborea; Pistia Stratiotes; Desmodium Gangeticum; Grislea Tomentosa; N. of another plant, commonly called Kaṭphala; N. of a deity; (ई), f. a plant, commonly called Kaṭphala. —कुमुद-खण्ड, अम्, n. an assemblage of Kumudas. —कुमुद-घ्नी, f., N. of a plant containing a poisonous milky juice. —कु-मुद-पत्त्राभ (°त्र-आभ), अस्, आ, अम्, resem-bling the leaves of the white water-lily. —कुमुद-बन्धु, उस्, m. or कुमुद-बान्धव, अस्, m. the moon (‘friend of the lotus;’ the white esculent lotus expanding its petals during the night and closing them in the day time; hence other similar appella-tions of the moon, as कुमुद-प्रिय, &c.). —कु-मुद-वती, f. an assemblage of Kumudas, a place abounding in them, &c. —कुमुद-सुहृद्, त्, m. the moon; [cf. कुमुद-बन्धु।] —कुमुदाकर (°द-आक्°), अस्, m. a number of water-lilies or place abounding in them. —कुमुदाक्ष (°द-अक्°), अस्, m., N. of a Nāga; also of an attendant of Viṣṇu. —कुमुदादि (°द-आदि), इस्, m., N. of a pupil of Pathya. —कुमुदावास (°द-आव्°), अस्, आ, अम्, abounding or richly furnished with Kumudas; (अस्), m. a pool abounding in them. —कुमुदेश (°द-ईश), अस्, m. an epithet of the moon, ‘lord of the lotus.’
कुमुदिक: कुमुदिक, अस्, ई, अम्, abounding with Kumudas; (इका), f., N. of a plant, commonly called Kaṭphala; a small tree, the seeds of which are aromatic.
कुमुदिनी: कुमुदिनी, f. an assemblage of Kumudas or a place abounding in them; the mother of Raghu-deva. —कुमुदिनी-नायक, अस्, m. or कुमुदिनी-पति, इस्, m. an epithet of the moon; [cf. कुमुद-बन्धु।] —कुमुदिनी-वनिता, f. any loved woman fancifully represented as an assemblage of lotus flowers.
कुमेधस्: कुमेधस् कु-मेधस्, आस्, आस्, अस् (see 1. कु), of little intellect, stupid; malicious.
कुमेरु: कुमेरु कु-मेरु, उस्, m. (see 1. कु), the southern hemisphere or pole, the region of the demons and Titans.
कुमोदक: कुमोदक कुमोदक, अस्, m. an epithet of Viṣṇu; [cf. कौमोदकी।]
कुम्प्: कुम्प् कुम्प्, cl. 10. P. कुम्पयति, -यितुम्, another form for कुम्ब्, कुम्बयति।
कुम्प: कुम्प कुम्प, अस्, आ, अम्, crooked-armed.
कुम्ब्: कुम्ब् कुम्ब्, cl. 6. and 10. P. कुम्बति and कुम्बयति, -यितुम्, to cover; [cf. कुम्प् and कुम्भ्।]
कुम्ब: कुम्ब कुम्ब, अस् or अम् (?), m. or n. (?), Ved. a kind of head-dress for women; the upper part or top of a club; (आ), f. a thick petticoat; an en-closure round a place of sacrifice to prevent profane intrusion.
कुम्बिक: कुम्बिक कुम्बिक, आस्, m. pl., N. of a people.
कुम्ब्या: कुम्ब्या कुम्ब्या or कुम्व्या, f., Ved. a kind of hymn or sacred formula.
कुम्भ्: कुम्भ् कुम्भ्, cl. 10. P. कुम्भयति, -यि-तुम्, another form for कुम्ब्, q. v.
कुम्भ: कुम्भ कुम्भ, अस्, m. a jar, pitcher, water-pot, ewer, a small water-jar, (often in compounds, e. g. छिद्र-कुम्भ, a perforated pitcher; आम-कुम्भ, a jar of unbaked clay; हेम-कुम्भ, a golden ewer; जल-कुम्भ, a water-pot); an urn in which the bones of a dead person are collected; the sign of the zodiac Aquarius; a measure of grain equal to twenty Droṇas, a little more than three bushels and three gallons (commonly called a comb, some make it two Droṇas or sixty-four Seers); the frontal globe on the upper part of the forehead of an elephant (there are two of these projections which swell in the rutting season); a religious exercise, viz. closing the nostrils and mouth so as to suspend breathing; the root of a plant used in medicine; the paramour of a harlot, a bully, a flash or fancy man; N. of a Muni; N. of a Dānava, son of Prahlāda and brother of Nikumbha; also of a Rākṣasa, a son of Kumbha-karṇa; N. of the father of the nineteenth Arhat of the present Avasar-piṇī; N. of a monkey; one of the thirty-four jātakas or former births of Śākya-muni; title of a work; (ई), f. a small jar or pot, an earthen cooking vessel; a vessel for preserving grain, a measure of grain; N. of several plants, a small tree, the seeds of which are used in medicine, commonly called Kaṭphala; an-other plant, Bignonia Suaveolens; another plant, Pistia Stratiotes; another plant, commonly called Romaśa; another plant, Croton Polyandrum; (आ), f. a harlot, a whore; (अम्), n. the plant Ipomœa Turpethum; a fragrant resin (गुग्गुलु), or the plant which bears it; [cf. Gr. κύμβη Lat. cymba.] —कुम्भ-कर्ण, अस्, m., N. of a Rākṣasa, the gigantic brother of Rāvaṇa, who is described in the Yuddha-kāṇḍa of the Rāmāyaṇa as sleeping for six months at a time, and then waking to gorge him-self; N. of a Muni; an epithet of Śiva; N. of a Dānava. —कुम्भकर्ण-वध, अस्, m. ‘the slaughter of Kumbhakarṇa,’ a section of the Padma-purāṇa. —कुम्भ-कामला, f. a bilious affection, a sort of jaundice together with swelling of the joints; [cf. कुम्भ-पाद।] —कुम्भ-कार, अस्, m. a potter, being according to some authorities the son of a Brāhman by a wife of the Kṣatriya caste; a serpent; a kind of wild fowl; (ई), f. the wife of a potter; N. of a girl; कुरु: कुरु कुरु, अवस्, m. pl. (said to be fr. 1. कृ), N. of a people of India and their country, situated near the country of the Pañcālas (hence often con-nected with Pañcāla or Pāñcāla; see कुरु-पञ्चाल below); the Kurus derive their origin from Kuru (son of Saṃvaraṇa and Tapatī, daughter of the Sun), who is the ancestor of both Pāṇḍu and Dhṛta-rāṣṭra, though the patronymic derived from his name is usually applied only to the sons of the latter, the sons and descendants of the former being called Pāṇḍavas; another Kuru is the son of Agnīdhra and grandson of Priya-vrata. The उत्तर-कुरवः or उत्तराः कुर-वः are the northern Kurus, the most northerly of the four Mahā-dvīpas or principal divisions of the known world (distinguished Mahā-bh. I. 4346. from the दक्-षिणाः कुरवः or southern Kurus), by other sys-tems regarded as one of nine divisions or Varṣas of the same; it was probably a country beyond the most northern range of the Himālaya, often described as a country of everlasting happiness, and considered by some to be the ancient home of the Āryan race. कुरू, ऊस्, f. a princess of the Kuru race. According to native lexicographers the word कुरु has also the following meanings; a priest; boiled rice; the plant Solanum Jacquini, = कण्टकारिक; [cf. कौरव, कौरवक, कौरव्य।] —कुरु-कत, आस्, m. pl. the Kurus and Katas. —कुरु-कन्दक, अम्, n. horse-radish, Raphanus Sativus (= मूलक). —कुरु-कुरुक्षेत्र, अम्, n. the country of the Kurus and Kurukṣetra. —कुरु-क्षेत्र, अम्, n. the field of the Kurus, N. of a region or extensive plain near Delhi, the scene of the great battles between the Kurus and Pāṇḍus; (आस्), m. pl. the inhabitants of this country, renowned for their bravery. —कुरु-क्षेत्रिन्, ई, इणी, इ, with योग, a solar day, in the course of which three lunar days, three asterisms and three yogas occur. —कुरु-चिल्ल, अस्, m. a crab; [cf. कुरचिल्ल।] —कुरु-जाङ्गल, अम्, n., N. of a country; (आस्), m. pl., N. of the people inhabiting it. —कुरु-तीर्थ, अम्, n., N. of a Tīrtha. —कुरु-नदिका, f. according to native authorities, = कु-न-दिका. —कुरु-नन्दन, अस्, m. a descendant of Kuru as Arjuna, Yudhiṣṭhira, &c. —कुरु-पञ्चाल, आस्, m. pl. the Kurus and Pañcālas. —कुरुपञ्चाल-त्रा, ind., Ved. as among the Kurus and Pañcālas. —कुरु-पथ, अस्, m., N. of a man (?); [cf. कौरुपथि।] —कुरु-पुङ्गव, अस्, m. a Kuru chief. —कुरु-राज्, ट्, m. an epithet of Duryodhana. —कुरु-राज, अस्, m. an epithet of Yudhiṣṭhira. —कुरु-राज्य, अम्, n. the Kuru realm. —कुरु-वत्स, अस्, m., N. of a prince. —कुरु-वर्णक, आस्, m. pl., N. of a people; or perhaps (अस्, आ, अम्), be-longing to the race of the Kurus. —कुरु-वश, अस्, m., N. of a prince. —कुरु-वाजपेय, अस्, m. a particular kind of Vājapeya. —कुरु-विस्त, अस्, m. a Pala of gold, a weight of gold equal to about 700 troy grains. —कुरु-वृद्ध, अस्, m. an epithet of Bhīṣma. —कुरु-श्रवण, अस्, m., N. of a prince. —कुरु-श्रेष्ठ or कुरु-सत्तम, अस्, m. an epi-thet of Arjuna. —कुरु-हार, अस् or अम् (?), m. or n. (?), N. of an Agra-hāra.

कुल्: कुल् कुल्, cl. 1. P. कोलति, चुकोल, &c., कोलितुम्, to accumulate, collect; to be of kin, to behave as a kinsman; to proceed continuously or without interruption; to count.
कुल: कुल कुल, अम्, n. (fr. rt. कुल्?), a herd, a troop, a flock, an assemblage, a multitude, a number &c. (of quadrupeds, birds, insects, &c., or of inanimate objects, e. g. गो-कुल, a herd of cows; मृग-कुल, a herd of deer; महिषी-कुल, a herd of female buffaloes; अलि-कुल, a swarm of bees; अलक-कुल, a multitude of curls); a race, family, community, tribe, caste, association, set, company (e. g. ब्राह्-मण-कुल, the caste of the Brāhmans); the resi-dence of a family, seat of a community; (in a contemptuous sense) a lot, a gang (forming a comp. with a preceding gen. sing., e. g. चौरस्य-कुल, a gang of thieves); an inhabited country; a house, an abode; a noble or eminent family or race; high station (often at the beginning of a compound = chief, principal; see कुल-गिरि below); the body; the front, fore part; a blue stone; (अस्), m. the chief of a corporation or guild; [cf. Hib. gaol, ‘a family or kindred.’] कुलि and कुली, see s. v. —कुल-कज्जल, अस्, m. disgrace of the family. —कुल-कण्टक, अस्, m. ‘a family-thorn,’ any one who is a trouble to his family. —कुल-कन्या, f. a girl of good family. —कुल-कर, अस्, ई, अम्, founding a family, the founder of a family or race, an ancestor. —कुल-कर्कटी, f. a kind of gourd; [cf. चीनाकर्कती।] —कुल-कर्तृ, ता, m. the founder of a family or race, an ancestor. —कुल-कर्मन्, अ, n. the peculiar or proper duty of a family or race, any observance or custom peculiar to a family. —कुल-कलङ्क, अस्, m. ‘a family-stain,’ any one who disgraces his family. —कुल-क्षय, अस्, m. decay or downfall of a race or family; (आ), f. a sort of cowach, Mucuna Pruritus (= शूकशिम्बी). —कुल-गरिमन्, आ, m. family pride. —कुल-गिरि, इस्, m. a chief mountain, any one of the seven principal mountains of Bhārata-varṣa; see कुलाचल. —कुल-गृह, अम्, n. a noble house. —कुल-गोप, अस्, m., Ved. the protector of a domicile. —कुल-गौरव, अम्, n. family import-ance. —कुल-घ्न, अस्, आ or ई, अम्, destroying a family. —कुल-चन्द्र, अस्, m., N. of a scholiast on the Kātantra grammar; N. of the author of the Durgāvākya-prabodha. —कुल-चूडामणि, title of a work. —कुल-च्युत, अस्, आ, अम्, rejected by his family. —कुल-ज or कुल-जात, अस्, आ, अम्, born in a noble family, of a good or noble family, well-born, of good breed; ancestral, hereditary. —कुल-जन, अस्, m. a person belonging to a noble family, a high-born or distinguished person. —कुल-तत्त्व-विद्, त्, त्, त्, knowing the true state of a family. —कुल-तस्, ind. by birth. —कुल-तिथि, इस्, m. f. an important lunar day, the fourth, eighth, twelfth, or fourteenth day of the half-month. —कुल-तिलक, अस्, m. the glory of a family, one who does honour to a family. —कुल-दमन, अस्, आ, अम्, subduing a family, holding it in subjection. —कुल-दीप or कुल-दीपक, अस्, m. the lamp or light or glory of a race or family; (इका), f. title of a work treating on the noble families of Bengal. —कुल-दुहितृ, ता, f. the daughter of a noble family; a high-born maiden. —कुल-देवता, f. a principal deity; an epithet of the goddess Durgā. —कुल-दैव, अम्, n. family destiny; a principal deity. —कुल-धर्म, अस्, m. practice or observance peculiar to a tribe or family, peculiar duty of caste or race. —कुल-धारक, अस्, m. ‘upholder of the family,’ a son. —कुल-धुर्य, अस्, m. one who is able to support a family, a grown-up son. —कुल-नक्षत्र, अम्, n. any Nakṣatra or lunar mansion distinguished above others; any auspicious asterism. —कुल-नन्दन, अस्, आ, अम्, causing joy to a family, doing honour to a family; a high-born virtuous child. —कुल-नायिका, f. a girl worshipped at the celebration of the orgies of the left-hand Śāktas. —कुल-नारी, f. a woman of good family; a high-bred virtuous woman. —कुल-नाश, अस्, m. a camel; a reprobate, an outcast. —कुल-निन्दा, f. family disgrace. —कुलन्-धर, अस्, आ, अम्, upholding a family. —कुल-प, अस्, m., Ved. the chief of a family or race or tribe. —कुल-पति, इस्, m. the head or chief of a family. —कुल-पत्त्र, अस्, m. a plant, commonly called Damanaka. —कुल-परम्परा, f. the series of generations comprising a race. —कुल-पर्वत or कुल-शैल, अस्, m. a principal mountain, any one of seven mountains in Bhārata; [cf. कुल-गिरि।] —कुल-पांसुका, f. an unchaste woman. —कुल-पालक, अस्, इका, अम्, pro-tecting a family, nourishing or providing for a family; (अम्), n. a kind of orange, = कुरुम्ब, commonly कमलानेवु. —कुल-पालि, इस्, f. or कुल-पालिका, f. or कुल-पाली, f. a chaste, high-born, or noble woman. —कुल-पुत्र, अस्, m. a son of a noble family, a noble or respectable youth; (ई), f. the daughter of a good family, a high-born or respectable girl; [cf. कुल-दुहितृ।] —कुल-पुत्रक, अस्, m., N. of a plant, = कुल-पत्त्र and मुनि-पुत्र। —कुलपुत्र-जन, अस्, m. the son of a good family, a noble or respectable youth. —कुल-पु-रुष, अस्, m. a man of good family, a noble or respectable man; an ancestor, any family progenitor. —कुल-पूर्वग, अस्, m. an ancestor. —कुल-प्रकाश, अस्, m. title of a work. —कुल-प्रसूत, अस्, आ, अम्, born in a noble family. —कुल-बधू, ऊस्, f. a noble, virtuous, or respectable woman; [cf. कु-ल-योषित्।] —कुल-बालिका, f. = कुल-पालिका above. —कुल-भार्या, f. a virtuous, noble, or high-bred wife. —कुल-भूभृत्, त्, m. a principal mountain, one of the seven mountains in Bhārata. —कुल-भूषण, अस्, आ, अम्, ‘family-adorning,’ a family ornament. —कुल-भृत्या, f. the nursing of a preg-nant woman; a midwife, a nurse?; [cf. कुमार-भृत्या।] —कुल-भेद-कर, अस्, m. one who causes discord in a family. —कुल-भ्रष्ट, अस्, आ, अम्, expelled from a family. —कुल-मर्यादा, f. family honour or respectability. —कुल-मार्ग, अस्, m. the best or principal way, the way of honesty. —कुल-मित्र, अम्, n. a friend of the family. —कु-लम्-पुन, अस्, आ, अम्, purifying a family; (अम्), n., N. of a Tīrtha; (आ), f., N. of a river. —कुलम्-भर, अस्, आ, अम्, carrying or upholding a family; (अस्), m. a wrong form for कुजम्भल, a thief. —कुल-योषित्, त्, f. a woman of noble family; a virtuous high-born woman. —कुल-रक्षक, अस्, आ, अम्, preserving a family. —कुल-रत्न-मालिका, f. title of a work. —कुल-वत्, आन्, अती, अत्, be-longing to a noble family. —कुल-वधू, ऊस्, f. a virtuous wife, a respectable woman, one of good family. —कुलवधू-ता, f. virtue in a wife. —कुल-वर्णा, f. a species of the plant Convolvulus with red blossoms, = रक्त-त्रिवृत्. —कुल-वर्धन or कुल-वर्धक, अस्, आ, अम्, increasing or advancing or propagating a family. —कुल-वार, अस्, m. a principal day, i. e. Tuesday and Friday. —कुल-विद्या, f. knowledge handed down in a family. —कुल-विप्र, अस्, m. a family priest. —कुल-वृद्ध, अस्, m. the oldest member or head of a family. —कुल-वृद्धि, इस्, f. family advancement. —कुल-व्यापिन्, ई, इनी, इ, attaching or applicable to tribe or caste. —कुल-व्रत, अम्, n. a family vow. —कुल-शील, अस्, अम्, m. n. character or conduct honourable to a family. —कुल-शील-समन्वित, अस्, आ, अम्, endowed with a noble character or disposi-tion. —कुल-शेखर, अस्, m., N. of the author of Mukunda-mālā. —कुल-श्रेष्ठिन्, ई, इनी, इ, well-born; of good family, eminent in a family; (ई), m. the chief of a guild; an artificer or artisan of eminent birth. —कुल-सङ्ख्या, f. ranking or being reckoned as a family, family respectability. —कुल-सत्त्र, अम्, n. a family sacrifice. —कुल-सन्तति, इस्, f. propa-gation of a family, posterity, descendants. —कुल-सन्निधि, इस्, m. the presence of a number of persons or of witnesses, kindred, relations. —कुल-समुद्-भव, अस्, आ, अम्, born in a noble family. —कुल-सम्भव, अस्, आ, अम्, sprung from a noble family; (in compounds) sprung from a family. —कुल-सार-तन्त्र, अम्, n., N. of a Tantra. —कुल-सुन्दरी, f., N. of a deity. —कुल-सेवक, अस्, m. an excellent attendant or servant. —कुल-सौरभ, अम्, n., N. of a plant, = मरुवक. —कुल-स्त्री, f. a woman of good family, a respectable woman, a chaste or virtuous wife. —कुल-स्थिति, इस्, f. antiquity or prosperity of a family. —कुलाकुल (°ल-अक्°), अस्, आ, अम्, excel-lent and not excellent, middling; of mixed character, of mixed origin; (अस्), m., N. of a Dānava. —कुला-कुल-तिथि, इस्, m. f. the second, sixth, and tenth lunar days of a half-month. —कुलाकुल-नक्षत्र, अम्, n., N. of the lunar mansions Ārdrā, Mūlā, Abhi-jit, and Śatabhiṣā; an asterism of mixed character. —कुलाकुल-वार, अस्, m. Wednesday. —कुलाङ्-गना (°ल-अङ्°), f. a woman of good family, a respectable or chaste woman. —कुलाङ्गार (°ल-अङ्°), अस्, m. ‘a family firebrand,’ metaphorically a man who foments domestic dissensions or ruins his family. —कुलाचल (°ल-अच्°), अस्, m. a principal mountain, one of a class of seven principal mountains which are supposed to exist in each Varṣa or division of a continent; those of Bhārata-varṣa or India are Mahendra, Malaya, Sahya, Śuktimat, Ṛkṣa, Vin-dhya, and Pāripātra or Pāriyātra; N. of a Dānava. —कुलाचार (°ल-आच्°), अस्, m. the peculiar or proper duty of a family or caste. —कुलाचार्य (°ल-आच्°), अस्, m. a family teacher, a family priest; a person well versed in the pedigrees and customs of different families and employed to contract marriages between them; a genealogist. —कुलाद्रि (°ल-अद्°), इस्, m. a principal mountain; one of seven principal mountains; see कुलाचल above. —कुलाधारक (°ल-आध्°), अस्, m. a son; [cf. कुल-धारक।] —कुलान्वित (°ल-अन्°), अस्, आ, अम्, sprung from a noble family. —कुला-भिमान (°ल-अभ्°), अम्, n. pride of birth, family pride. —कुलाभिमानिन्, ई, इनी, इ, proud of birth or of family descent. —कुलामृत (°ल-अम्°), अम्, n. title of a work. —कुलार्णव (°ल-अर्°), अस्, m. title of a work. —कुलार्णव-तन्त्र, अम्, n., N. of a Tantra. —कुलालम्बिन् (°ल-आल्°), ई, इनी, इ, supporting or maintaining a family. —कुले-चर, अस् or अम् (?), m. or n. (?) , a kind of plant. —कुलेश्वर (°ल-ईश्°), अस्, m. the chief of a family or race; the lord κατ᾽ ἐξοχήν, an epithet of Śiva; (ई), f. an epithet of Durgā. —कु-लोत्कट (°ल-उत्°), अस्, आ, अम्, excellent by birth, high-born; (अस्), m. a horse of good breed. —कुलोत्-कर्ष (°ल-उत्°), अस्, m. family eminence. —कुलोत्-पन्न (°ल-उत्°), अस्, आ, अम्, sprung from a good family, well-born; belonging to a family (as property &c.). —कुलोद्गत (°ल-उद्°), अस्, आ, अम्, sprung from a noble family. —कुलोद्भव, अस्, आ, अम्, or कुलोद्भूत (°ल-उद्°), अस्, आ, अम्, well-born, of good family; born or produced in a family. —कुलोद्-वह (°ल-उद्°), अस्, m. a chief, a leader, the head of a family. —कुलोपदेश (°ल-उप्°), अस्, m. family name.
कुल, अम्, n.; add — (with Śāktas), epithet of Śakti and of the rites observed in her worship [cf. कौल].
कुलक: कुलक, अस्, आ, अम्, relating to a tribe or family, of good family, of eminent birth; (अस्), m. the chief of a guild; any artisan of eminent birth; an ant-hill, a mole-hill; a green snake (हरित-सर्प); N. of several plants, a kind of ebony, Diospyros Tomentosa; another species of ebony, commonly called Ku-pīlu; another plant, = मरुवक, शुक्लपुष्प, तिलक; (अम्), n. a multitude; a sort of gourd, Trichosanthes Diœca; a number of stanzas in grammatical con-nection, several verses in which the government of noun and verb is carried throughout, contrary to the practice of closing the sense with each verse; a kind of prose composition with few compound words.
कुलायन: कुलायन, अस्, m., N. of a man.
कुलिक: कुलिक, अस्, आ, अम्, of a good family, well-born; (अस्), m. a kinsman; the chief or head man of a tribe or caste; an artist or artificer of high birth; a thorny plant, Ruellia Longifolia or Asteracantha (Ruellia) Longifolia; one of the eight chiefs of the Nāgas or serpent-race, described as having a half-moon on the top of his head and being of a dusky-brown colour. —कुलिक-वेला, f. certain portions of each day on which it is improper to begin any good business.
कुलिन्: कुलिन्, ई, इनी, इ, belonging to a noble family.
कुलीन: कुलीन, अस्, आ, अम् (at the end of compounds), belonging to a family; of high or eminent descent, of a good family, well-born; (अस्), m. a horse of good breed; a Brāhman of the highest class in Ben-gal, i. e. a member of one of the eight principal families of the Vārendra division or of one of the six chief families of the Rāḍha or Rāṛh division as classified by Balāl Sen, Rāja of Bengal, in the twelfth century, (common names of the latter families are Mukharji, Banarji, Chatoji, &c.); a worshipper of Śakti according to the left-hand ritual; (आ), f. a variety of the Āryā metre; (अम्), n. a disease of the nails. —कुलीन-ता, f. or कुलीन-त्व, अम्, n. birth, rank, family respectability.
कुलीनक: कुलीनक, अस्, आ, अम्, of good family; (अस्), m. a kind of wild kidney-bean.
कुलेय: कुलेय, अस्, आ, अम् (at the end of compounds) = कुलीन।
कुल्य: 1. कुल्य, अस्, आ, अम्, of or relating to a family or race; belonging to a congregation or corporation; of good family, well-born, well-descended; (अस्), m. a respectable man; (आ), f. a virtuous or decent woman; custom or habit of a family?; (अम्), n. friendly in-quiry after family affairs or domestic accidents, con-dolence, congratulation, &c. (For 2. 3. see col. 3.)
कुल्य 2. कुल्य, अम्, n. (for 1. कुल्य see col. 1), a bone; flesh; a winnowing basket; a measure of eight Droṇas.
3. कुल्य, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. belonging to a river.
कुलक्क: कुलक्क कुलक्क, अस्, m. a cymbal; beating time in music.
कुलङ्गी: कुलङ्गी कुलङ्गी, f. a thorny plant; (a wrong form for कुलिङ्गी।)
कुलञ्ज: कुलञ्ज कुलञ्ज or कुलञ्जन, अस्, m. the plant Alpinia Galanga, = गन्ध-मूल।
कुलट: कुलट कुलट, अस्, m. (fr. कुल and rt. अट्?), any son except one's own offspring, an adopted son, a bought son, &c.; (आ), f. an unchaste woman. —कुलटा-पति, इस्, m. the husband of an unchaste woman, a cuckold.
कुलटी: कुलटी कुलटी, f. red arsenic, = कुनटी।
कुलति: कुलति कुलति, अयस्, m. pl., N. of a people.
कुलत्थ: कुलत्थ कुलत्थ, अस्, m. (fr. कुल? cf. अश्-वत्थ and कपित्थ), a kind of pulse, Dolichos Uniflorus; (आस्), m. pl., N. of a people; (आ), f. a kind of Dolichos; a blue stone used in medicine and ap-plied as a collyrium to the eyes, also as an astringent to sores &c.; a species of metre.
कुलत्थिका: कुलत्थिका, f. a blue stone used as a collyrium &c.; a sort of vetch, considered as a wild sort of the Dolichos Uniflorus.
कुलभ: कुलभ कुलभ, अस्, m., N. of a Daitya; (another reading has सुलभ।)
कुलहण्डक: कुलहण्डक कुलहण्डक, अस्, m. an eddy, = कूलहण्डक।
कुलाट: कुलाट कुलाट, अस्, m. a kind of small fish.
कुलाद्य: कुलाद्य कुलाद्य, अस्, m. (?), N. of a country or people.
कुलाभि: कुलाभि कुलाभि, इस्, m. a treasure.
कुलाय: कुलाय कुलाय, अस्, अम्, m. n. (fr. कुल?), a woven texture, a web; the nest of a bird; a case or investing integument, a receptacle; the body as the dwelling-place of the soul; the kennel or resting-place of a dog &c.; a place, a spot in general. —कुलाय-निलाय, अस्, m. the act of sitting in a nest, hatching, brooding. —कुलायनिलायि-ता, f. the act or state of hatching, &c. —कुलाय-निलायिन्, ई, इनी, इ, sitting in a nest, brooding, hatching. —कुलाय-स्थ, अस्, m. ‘nest-dweller,’ a bird.
कुलाययत्: कुलाययत्, अन्, अन्ती, अत् (fr. nom. कुलायय), Ved. building nests or a resting-place, hiding one's self in a nest.
कुलायिका: कुलायिका, f. a bird-cage, an aviary.
कुलायिन्: कुलायिन्, ई, इनी, इ, Ved. forming a nest, shaped like a nest, homely; (इनी), f., N. of a liturgical service.
कुलाल: कुलाल कुलाल, अस्, m. (said to be fr. rt. कुल्), a potter; a wild cock, Phasianus Gallus; an owl; (ई), f. the wife of a potter; N. of a plant; a species of blue stone applied as a collyrium to the eyes (कुलत्थिका). —कुलाल-वत्, ind. like a potter.
कुलालिका: कुलालिका कुलालिका, f. an aviary; (a wrong form for कुलायिका।)
कुलाह: कुलाह कुलाह, अस्, m. a horse of a light-brown colour with black knees.
कुलाहक: कुलाहक कुलाहक, अस्, m. a lizard, a chame-lion; N. of a plant, commonly Rāṅgā Kulekhāḍā.
कुलाहल: कुलाहल कुलाहल, अस्, m., N. of a plant, = अलम्बुष, गोच्छाल, भूकदम्ब, commonly Kokaśimā, Coryza Terebinthina or Celsia Coroman-delina, (a plant which dogs are fond of smelling before they eject urine.)
कुलि: कुलि कुलि, इस्, m. the hand; (इस्), f., N. of a plant, = कण्टकारी, a prickly nightshade.
कुलिङ्ग: कुलिङ्ग कु-लिङ्ग, अस्, m. (see 1. कु), a kind of mouse; a species of bird, the fork-tailed shrike; N. of a man; (आ), f., N. of a town; (ई), f., N. of a plant [cf. कर्कट-शृङ्गी]; the female of the fork-tailed shrike. —कुलिङ्गाक्षी (°ग-अक्°), f., N. of a plant, = पेटिका, कुवेराक्षी।
कुलिज: कुलिज कुलिज, अस् or अम् (?), m. or n. (?), a sort of measure (occurring at the end of com-pounds in the forms कुलिज, अस्, ई, अम्; कुलिजिक, अस्, ई, अम्; कुलिजीन, अस्, आ, अम्).
कुलिन्द: कुलिन्द कुलिन्द, आस्, m. pl., N. of a people; (अस्), m. sing. the prince of this people.
कुलिर: कुलिर कुलिर, अस्, m. a crab; also कुलीर, q. v.
कुलिश: कुलिश कुलिश, अस्, अम्, m. n. कुली: कुली कुली, f. a wife's elder sister; the plant Solanum Jacquini or Solanum Longum (वृ-हती).

कुवाहुल: कुवाहुल कुवाहुल, अस्, m. a camel.
कुविक: कुविक कुविक, आस्, m. pl., N. of a people.

कुशीलव: कुशीलव कुशीलव, अस्, m. (connected with कु-शील?), a bard, herald; an actor, dancer, mime; a newsmonger; an epithet of Vālmīki; (औ), m. du. the two sons of Rāma, Kuśa and Lava, who recited the Rāmāyaṇa, (probably these names were originally formed from the word Kuśīlava); [cf. कुश-लव।]
कुशीवश: कुशीवश कुशीवश, अस्, m. an epithet of Vālmīki; [cf. कुशिन् and कुशीलव।]
कुशुम्भ: कुशुम्भ कुशुम्भ, अस्, m. a jar; the water-pot of an ascetic; [cf. कुसुम्भ।]
कुशूल: कुशूल कुशूल, अस्, m. कुश्रि: कुश्रि कुश्रि, इस्, m., N. of a teacher.
कुश्रुत: कुश्रुत कु-श्रुत, अस्, आ, अम् (see 1. कु), in-distinctly heard.
कुश्वभ्र: कुश्वभ्र कु-श्वभ्र, अम्, n. (see 1. कु), a small hole.
कुष्: कुष् कुष्, cl. 9. P. कुष्णाति, चुकोष, कोषिष्यति, अकोषीत्, कोषितुम्, to tear, tear asunder, to force or draw out, to extract, to expel; to test, assay, examine; to shine: Pass. कुष्यति and कुष्यते: Caus. कोषयति: Desid. चुकोषि-षति and चुकुषिषति: Intens. चोकुष्यते, चो-कोष्टि।
कुषण्ड: कुषण्ड कु-षण्ड, अस्, m. (see 1. कु), N. of a priest.
कुषल: कुषल कुषल, अस्, आ, अम्, clever, expert, &c.; (a wrong reading for कुशल।)
कुषवा: कुषवा कुषवा, f., Ved., N. of a Rākṣasī.
कुषाकु: कुषाकु कुषाकु, उस्, उस्, उ (fr. rt. कुष्?), burning, scorching, inflaming; wicked, detestable; (उस्), m. fire; the sun; a monkey; [cf. कषाकु।]
कुषारु: कुषारु कुषारु, उस्, m., N. of a man.
कुषित: कुषित कुषित, अस्, आ, अम्, mixed with water [cf. कुशित]; (अम्), n. happy, well, right, fortunate, auspicious, &c. (?).
कुषीतक: कुषीतक कुषीतक, अस्, m., Ved. a kind of bird; N. of a man; (आस्), m. pl. the descendants of this man.
कुषीद: कुषीद कु-षीद, अस्, आ, अम्, indifferent, apa-thetic, inert; (अम्), n. usury; (more correctly कु-सीद।)
कुषीदिन्: कुषीदिन् कुषीदिन्, ई, m., N. of a teacher.
कुषुभ्य: कुषुभ्य कुषुभ्य, nom. P. कुषुभ्यति, to throw; to abuse; to despise.
कुषुम्भ: कुषुम्भ कुषुम्भ, अस्, m., Ved. the poison-bag of an insect.
कुष्ठ: कुष्ठ कुष्ठ, अस् or अम्, m. or n. (fr. 1. कु and स्थ?), a sort of medicinal plant (used as a remedy for the disease called तक्मन्, q. v.), Costus Speciosus or Arabicus; a sort of poison; leprosy, of which eighteen varieties are enumerated, seven severe and eleven of minor importance; (आ), f. the mouth or open-ing of a basket. —कुष्ठ-केतु, उस्, m., N. of a plant, = भूम्याहुल्य. —कुष्ठ-गन्धि, n. the fra-grant bark of the plant Feronia Elephantum. —कुष्-ठ-घ्न, अस्, ई, अम्, curing leprosy; (अस्), m., N. of a medicinal plant, commonly called Hiyāvalī [cf. हितावली]; (ई), f. an esculent root, Solanum Indicum, = काकमाची; the opposite leaved fig tree. —कुष्-ठ-चिकित्सित, अम्, n. the cure of leprosy. —कुष्ठ-नाशन, अस्, m., N. of several plants which cure leprosy; the root of Dioscorea; white pepper or mustard; another plant, = क्षीरीश-वृक्ष. —कु-ष्ठ-नाशिनी, f. a plant, commonly Hākuca, Psoralia Corylifolia. —कुष्ठ-मय, अस्, ई, अम्, full of leprosy, leprous. —कुष्ठ-रोग, अस्, m. leprosy, elephantiasis. —कुष्ठ-सूदन, अस्, m. the Cassia tree, Cassia Fistula; [cf. आरग्बध।] —कुष्ठ-हन्तृ, ता, m. a kind of bulbous plant, = हस्ति-कन्द; (त्री), f. another plant, generally called Vākucī. —कुष्ठ-हृत्, त्, m. the plant Acacia Catechu. —कुष्ठाङ्ग (°ठ-अङ्°), अस्, आ, अम्, leprous. —कुष्ठान्वित (°ठ-अन्°), अस्, आ, अम्, afflicted with leprosy. —कुष्ठारि (°ठ-अरि), इस्, m. Acacia Catechu; another plant, Acacia Farnesiana (विट्खदिर); another plant, Trichosanthes Diœca, = पटोल; another plant, = आदित्य-पत्त्र and अर्क-पत्त्र; sulphur.
कुष्ठित: कुष्ठित, अस्, आ, अम्, or कुष्ठिन्, ई, इनी, इ, leprous, a leper.
कुष्ठल: कुष्ठल कु-ष्ठल, अम्, n. (fr. 1. or 2. कु and स्थल), a bad place or spot; the surface of the earth.
कुष्ठिका: कुष्ठिका कुष्ठिका, आस्, f. pl. (related to कुष्-ठा?), Ved. a part of the foot of a sacrificial animal considered worthless for sacrificial purposes; (Sāy.) the contents of the entrails.
कुष्मल: कुष्मल कुष्मल, अम्, n. (said to be fr. rt. कुष्), cutting, dividing; a leaf.
कुष्माण्ड: कुष्माण्ड कुष्माण्ड, अस्, m. a kind of pump-kin-gourd, Benincasa Cerifera; false conception; a state of the womb in gestation (?); a particular re-ligious formula; a class of demons; one of a class of demi-gods attached to Śiva; (ई), f. the gourd Be-nincasa Cerifera, a drug; a religious ceremony, a certain rite, performed as a penance or expiation; an epithet of the wife of Śiva.
कुष्माण्डक: कुष्माण्डक, अस्, m. the gourd Benincasa Ceri-fera; N. of a Nāga; N. of an attendant of Śiva.
कुस्: कुस् कुस्, cl. 4. P. कुस्यति, to embrace, surround; [cf. कुश्।]
कुसचिव: कुसचिव कु-सचिव, अस्, m. (see 1. कु), a bad counsellor.
कुसरित्: कुसरित् कु-सरित्, त्, f. (see 1. कु), a shallow stream.
कुसलम्: कुसलम् कुसलम्, ind. well, happy, &c.; (more correctly कुशल, q. v.)
कुसहाय: कुसहाय कु-सहाय, अस्, m. (see 1. कु), a bad companion.
कुसारथि: कुसारथि कु-सारथि, इस्, m. (see 1. कु), a bad charioteer.
कुसित: कुसित कुसित, अस्, m. (said to be fr. कुस्), an inhabited country; N. of a country; a money-lender (?), see कुसीद. —कुसितायी, f. the wife of a money-lender (?); [cf. the following.]
कुसिदायी: कुसिदायी कुसिदायी, f. the wife of a Kusida, of a money-lender (?), see कुसीदायी; a kind of demon (?).
कुसिन्ध: कुसिन्ध कुसिन्ध, अम्, n., Ved. a trunk.
कुसीद: कुसीद कु-सीद, अस्, आ, अम् (see 1. कु), Ved. sitting too long in one spot (?), lazy, slothful, inert; (अम्), n. any loan or thing lent to be repaid with interest; lending money; usury, the profession of usury; (अस्, आ), m. f. a money-lender, a usurer. —कुसीद-पथ, अस्, m. usury, usurious interest, any exceeding five per cent. —कुसीद-वृद्धि, इस्, f. interest on money.
कुसीदायी: कुसीदायी, f. the wife of a usurer.
कुसीदिक: कुसीदिक, अस्, ई, अम्, one who follows the pro-fession of usury.
कुसीदिन्: कुसीदिन्, ई, m. a usurer; N. of a descendant of Kaṇva, author of several hymns of the Ṛg-veda.
कुसुम: कुसुम कुसुम, अस्, अम्, m. n. (said to be fr. rt. कुस्), a flower; (अम्), n. fruit; the menstrual dis-charge; a term for the shorter sections of Deveśvara's Kavi-kalpalatā (the longer chapters being called Stavaka); ophthalmia, disease of the eyes; (अस्), m. a form of fire; N. of the attendant of the sixth Arhat of the present Avasarpiṇī. —कुसुम-कार्-मुक or कुसुम-चाप, अस्, m. or कुसुम-धन्-वन्, आ, m. ‘having flowers for his bow,’ epithet of Kāma, the god of love. —कुसुम-केतुमण्डलिन्, ई, m., N. of a Kinnara. —कुसुम-कोमल, अस्, आ, अम्, tender as a flower. —कुसुम-चित, अस्, आ, अम्, heaped with flowers. —कुसुम-देव, अस्, m., N. of an author. —कुसुम-नग, अस्, m., N. of a mountain. —कुसुम-पुर, अम्, n., N. of the town Pāṭali-putra. —कुसुम-मध्य, अम्, n., N. of a tree bearing a large acid fruit, commonly Cālitā gāc, Cor-dia Myxa or Dillenia Indica. —कुसुम-मय, अस्, ई, अम्, consisting of flowers. —कुसुम-लता, f. a creeper in blossom. —कुसुम-वत्, आन्, अती, अत्, fur-nished with flowers, flowering, in flower; (ती), f. a female during menstruation; N. of the town Pāṭali-putra. —कुसुम-वाण, अस्, m. the flower-arrow of the god of love; ‘flower-arrowed,’ epithet of Kāma, the god of love, as having flowers for arrows. —कु-सुम-विचित्रा, f., N. of a metre consisting of four lines of twelve syllables each. —कुसुम-शयन, अम्, n. a couch of flowers. —कुसुम-शर, अस्, आ, अम्, ‘flower-arrowed,’ epithet of the god of love. —कुसुमशर-त्व, अम्, n. the state of one who has flowers for arrows. —कुसुम-शेखर-विजय, अस्, m. title of a play. —कुसुम-सनाथ, अस्, आ, अम्, possessed of flowers, having flowers. —कुसुम-स्तवक, अस्, m. a bunch of flowers, a nosegay, bou-quet, a garland; N. of a metre. —कुसुमाकर (°म-आक्°), अस्, m. a quantity of flowers or place abounding with them, a parterre, a garden, a nosegay; spring, the vernal season. —कुसुमाञ्जन (°म-अञ्°), अम्, n. the calx of brass, used as a collyrium. —कुसुमाञ्जलि (°म-अञ्°), इस्, f. ‘handful of flow-ers,’ the title of a philosophical work written to prove the existence of a Supreme being, by Udayana Āchārya, consisting of seventy-two Kārikās divided into five chapters. —कुसुमाञ्जलि-मकरन्द, अस्, m. title of a commentary by Rucidatta on the preceding work. —कुसुमात्मक (°म-आत्°), अम्, n. saffron. —कु-सुमाधिप (°म-अध्°), अस्, m. ‘the prince of flowers,’ the champa, a tree which bears a yellow fragrant flower, Michelia Champaka. —कुसुमा-धिराज् (°म-अध्°), ट्, m. the same plant. —कु-सुमायुध (°म-आय्°), अस्, m. ‘flower-armed,’ an epithet of Kāma, the god of love, his arrows being tipped with flowers. —कुसुमावचाय (°म-अव्°), अस्, m. gathering flowers. —कुसुमावतंसक (°म-अव्°), अम्, n. a chaplet, a crown of flowers. —कुसु-मावली (°म-अव्°), f. title of a medicinal work. —कुसुमासव (°म-आस्°), अम्, n. honey. —कु-सुमास्त्र (°म-अस्°), अस्, m. ‘flower-arrowed,’ epi-thet of the god of love. —कुसुमेषु (°म-इषु), उस्, m. = कुसुमास्त्र above; (उ), n. the bow of Kāma. —कुसुमोज्ज्वल (°म-उज्°), अस्, आ, अम्, bril-liant with blossoms.
कुसुमय: कुसुमय, nom. P. कुसुमयति, -यितुम्, to pro-duce flowers, cause to flower.
कुसुमित: कुसुमित, अस्, आ, अम्, furnished with flowers, flowered, budded, in flower. —कुसुमित-लता, f. or कुसुमितलता-वेल्लिता, f., N. of a metre consisting of four lines of eighteen syllables each.
कुसुम्य: कुसुम्य, nom. P. कुसुम्यति, to begin to flower.
कुसुमाल: कुसुमाल कुसुमाल, अस्, m. a thief (fr. कु-सुम + आल, ‘living among flowers?’).
कुसुम्भ: कुसुम्भ कुसुम्भ, अस्, अम्, m. n. (said to be fr. rt. कुस्), safflower, Carthamus Tinctorius; saffron, Crocus Sativus; the water-pot of the student and Sannyāsin; (अम्), n. gold; (अस्), m. outward affec-tion, compared with the colour of safflower; N. of a mountain. —कुसुम्भ-वत्, आन्, अती, अत्, furnished with a jar or water-pot.
कुसुरुविन्द: कुसुरुविन्द कुसुरुविन्द or कुसुरुबिन्द, अस्, m., N. of a descendant of Uddālaka.
कुसुरुबिन्दु: कुसुरुबिन्दु or कुसुरुविन्दु, उस्, m., N. of an author of several verses of the Vājasaneyi-saṃhitā.
कुसू: कुसू कुसू, ऊस्, m. an earth-worm.
कुसूल: कुसूल कुसूल, अस्, m., Ved. a kind of spiri-tual or supernatural being; a granary &c. See कुशूल।
कुसृति: कुसृति कु-सृति, इस्, f. (see 1. कु), evil con-duct, wickedness, depravity; conjuring, sleight-of-hand, magic; (इस्, इस्, इ), going evil ways, wicked.
कुस्तुभ: कुस्तुभ कुस्तुभ, अस्, m. an epithet of Viṣṇu (derived fr. कौस्तुभ?).
कुस्तुम्बरी: कुस्तुम्बरी कुस्तुम्बरी, f. a pungent seed used in condiments, coriander.
कुस्तुम्बरु: कुस्तुम्बरु कुस्तुम्बरु, उस्, m., N. of one of Kubera's attendants.
कुस्तुम्बुरु: कुस्तुम्बुरु कुस्तुम्बुरु, उस्, m. (said to be fr. 1. कु and तुम्बुरु), the plant coriander; (उ), n. the seed of this plant.
कुस्त्री: कुस्त्री कु-स्त्री, f. (see 1. कु), a bad woman.
कुस्मय: कुस्मय कुस्मय (fr. कु-स्मय), nom. A. कुस्मयते, to smile improperly; to see mentally, guess; to perceive, to imagine.
कुस्वप्न: कुस्वप्न कु-स्वप्न, अस्, m. (see 1. कु), a bad dream, a nightmare.
कुस्वामिन्: कुस्वामिन् कु-स्वामिन्, ई, m. (see 1. कु), a bad master.
कुह्: कुह् कुह्, cl. 10. A. कुहयते, -यितुम्, to surprise, astonish; to excite wonder, to cheat, to deceive by trickery or jugglery, impose upon (related to गुह्?).
कुह: 1. कुह, अस्, m. an epithet of Kuvera; a rogue, a cheat (in अ-कुह, q. v.).
कुह 2. कुह, ind. (fr. 1. कु), Ved. where? कुह चिद्, wherever, anywhere, somewhere, to any place. —कुहचिद्-विद्, त्, त्, त्, Ved. being everywhere.
कुहक: कुहक, अस्, आ, अम्, cheating, a cheat, a rogue, a juggler; (अस्), m. a frog; N. of a king of the serpent-race; (अम्, आ), n. f. juggling, deception, sleight-of-hand, legerdemain. —कुहक-कार, अस्, ई, अम्, or कुहक-कारक, अस्, इका, अम्, or कुहक-कारिन्, ई, इणी, इ, practising jugglery or conjuring, cheating. —कुहक-चकित, अस्, आ, अम्, afraid of a trick, suspicious, cautious, wary. —कुहक-जीविन्, ई, इनी, इ, living by sleight-of-hand, a conjurer, a cheat, &c. —कुहक-वृत्ति, इस्, f. juggling, conjuring, sleight-of-hand; hypocrisy.
कुहन: कुहन, अस्, आ, अम्, envious, hypocritical; (अस्), m. a mouse, a rat; a snake; N. of a man; (आ), f. hypocrisy; assumed and false sanctity; the interested performance of religious austerities; (अम्), n. a small earthen vessel; a glass vessel.
कुहया: कुहया, ind., Ved. where? —कुहया-कृति, इस्, इस्, इ, Ved. where active?
कुहकस्वन: कुहकस्वन कुहक-स्वन or कुहक-स्वर, अस्, m. (कुहक being here an onomatopoetic word), a wild cock, Phasianus Gallus.
कुहर: कुहर कुहर, अस्, m. (fr. कुह् = गुह्?), N. of a serpent belonging to the Krodhavaśa race; (अम्), n. a cavity, hollow; a hole, rent; the ear; the throat or larynx; a guttural sound; proximity; copulation.
कुहरित: कुहरित कुहरित, अम्, n. noise, a sound in general; especially the song or cry of the Kokila or Indian cuckoo; a sound uttered in copulation.
कुहलि: कुहलि कुहलि, इस्, m. the leaf of the Piper Betel (commonly called Pān) with small pieces of the Areca-nut and Catechu and a little lime, which are chewed and eaten by the people of the East and especially offered to the persons present at a matri-monial ceremony.
कुहा: कुहा कुहा, f., N. of a plant, also called Kaṭukī. —कुहा-वती, f. an epithet of the goddess Durgā.
कुहारीत: कुहारीत कु-हारीत, अस्, m. (see 1. कु), N. of a man.
कुहु: कुहु कुहु, उस्, f. the new moon; N. of a river; the cry of the Kokila; [cf. कुहू।]
कुहुकुहाय: कुहुकुहाय कुहुकुहाय (fr. कुहु-कुह for कुह-कुह, where? where?), nom. A. कुहुकुहा-यते, to show one's admiration.
कुहू: कुहू कुहू, ऊस्, f. कुहूल: कुहूल कुहूल, अम्, n. a pit filled with stakes.
कुहेडिका: कुहेडिका कुहेडिका or कुहेडी or कुहेलिका, f. a fog, a mist, haze, haziness.
कुह्वान: कुह्वान कु-ह्वान, अम्, n. (see 1. कु), a dis-agreeable noise.

कू 2. कू, ऊस्, f. a female Piśāca or goblin.
कूकुद: कूकुद कूकुद, अस्, m. one who gives a girl in marriage with due ceremony and suitable decora-tions.

कूचका: कूचका कूचका, f. the milky juice of a bulbous plant; [? cf. कूर्चिका।]
कूचक्र: कूचक्र कूचक्र, अस् or अम्? m. or n.? (for कु-चक्र), Ved. the female breast.

कूची: कूची कूची, f. a paint brush, a pencil; [cf. कूचिका and कूर्चिका।]
कूच्छलिङ्ग: कूच्छलिङ्ग कूच्छलिङ्ग, औ, m. du. = कु-कुन्दर, q. v.
कूज्: कूज् कूज्, cl. 1. कूज: कूज, अस्, m. rumbling (as of the bowels &c.); cooing, murmuring, a warbling &c.
कूजक: कूजक, अस्, इका, अम्, cooing, warbling, sounding, &c.
कूजत्: कूजत्, अन्, अन्ती, अत्, cooing, warbling, &c.
कूजन: कूजन, अम्, n. rumbling of the bowels; the uttering of any inarticulate sound, cooing, moaning; the rattling of wheels.
कूजित: कूजित, अस्, आ, अम्, uttered inarticulately, cooed, &c.; (अम्), n. the cry of a bird, cooing, warbling, &c.
कूजिन्: कूजिन्, ई, इनी, इ, making a rumbling sound in the bowels; warbling.
कूट्: कूट् कूट्, cl. 10. P. कूटयति, to burn; to give pain, be distressed, to call, invite; to counsel, advise; A. कूटयते, to avoid or decline giving, not to give; to render indistinct or unin-telligible, to muddle, to render confused or foul; to be distressed; to despair; [cf. Eng. heat, hot; Old Island. hiti, heitr; Germ. hitze, heiss.]
कूट: कूट कूट, अस्, अम्, m. n. the bone of the forehead with its projections or prominences, a horn; the crown of the head; any prominence or projec-tion (e. g. अंस-कूट, the hump of a buffalo; अक्षि-कूट, the prominence of the forehead above the eye); summit, the peak or summit of a mountain; summit, head, i. e. the highest, the most excellent, the first; a heap, a multitude (e. g. अभ्र-कूट, a multitude of clouds); a kind of vessel or implement; a hammer, an iron mallet; part of a plough, a ploughshare, the body of a plough; a trap for catching deer; a con-cealed weapon as a dagger in a wooden case, a sword-stick &c.; illusion, fraud, trick, deceit; a roguish scheme or plot; a knotty point, a puzzling question, an enigma, an obscure passage; untruth, falsehood, (or attributively) false, untrue; vile, low; uniform substance (as the ethereal element &c.); a water-jar; a kind of plant; (अस्, ई), m. f. a house, a dwelling [cf. कुट and कुटी]; (अस्), m. an epithet of Agastya; (अस्, आ, अम्), Ved. not horned or cornuted, as an animal with incomplete continuations of the bone of the forehead; (अस्), m. an ox whose horns are broken. —कूट-कार, अस्, m. a rogue, a cheat, a false witness. —कूट-कारक, अस्, इका, अम्, a rogue, a cheat, a false witness. —कूट-कृत्, त्, त्, त्, cheating, committing a fraud, bribing; (त्), m. a Kāyastha or man of the writer-caste; an epithet of Śiva. —कूट-खड्ग, अस्, m. a hidden sword, a sword-stick. —कूट-ग्रन्थ, title of a work supposed to be written by Vyāsa. —कूट-च्छद्मन्, आ, m. a rogue, a cheat. —कूट-ता, f. or कूट-त्व, अम्, n. falsehood, fraud. —कूट-तूला, f. a false pair of scales. —कूट-धर्म, अस्, आ, अम्, (a country or house) where falsehood is considered a duty. —कूट-पर्व or कूट-पूर्व, अस्, m. fever occurring in an elephant from vitiation of the three humors; (more correctly कूट-पूर्व।) —कूट-पालक, अस्, m. a bilious fever; a potter's kiln. —कूट-पाश, अस्, m. a trap. —कूट-बन्ध, अस्, m. a trap. —कूट-मान, अम्, n. a false measure or weight. —कूट-मुद्गर, अस्, m. a concealed weapon similar to a hammer. —कूट-मोहन, अस्, m. an epithet of Skanda. —कूट-यन्त्र, अम्, n. a trap or snare for deer, birds, &c. —कूट-युद्ध, अम्, n. a treacherous or unfair battle; (अस्, आ, अम्), fighting treacherously. —कूट-योधिन्, ई, इनी, इ, fighting unfairly or treacherously. —कूट-रचना, f. a laid trap. —कूट-शस्, ind. in heaps, in multitudes, by crowds. —कूट-शाल्मलि, इस्, m. f. or इका, f. a fabulous cotton-plant with sharp thorns, with which the wicked are tortured in the world of Yama; a species of the Simul silk-cotton tree. —कूट-शासन, अम्, n. a forged or false grant or decree. —कूट-शैल, अस्, m., N. of a mountain. —कूट-साक्षिन्, ई, m. a false witness. —कूट-स्थ, अस्, आ, अम्, standing at the top, keeping the highest position; standing in a multitude, standing in the midst; (in phil.) immovable, uniform, unchangeable, perpetually and universally the same, as the soul, spirit, space, ether, sound, &c.; (अम्), n. a sort of perfume, a species of dried shell-fish, commonly Nakhi; the soul. —कूटस्थ-ता, f. or कूटस्थ-त्व, अम्, n. unchangeableness, uniformity. —कूट-स्वर्ण, अम्, n. alloyed or counterfeit gold. —कूटा-क्ष (°ट-अक्°), अस्, m. loaded or false dice. —कूटा-गार (°ट-आग्°), अम्, n. an upper room, an apartment on the top of a house. —कूटार्थ (°ट-अर्°), अस्, m. ambiguity of meaning, fiction. —कूटार्थ-भा-षिता, f., scil. कथा, a tale, a story, a fiction. —कू-टोपाय (°ट-उप्°), अस्, m. trick, fraud, stratagem.

कूड्: कूड् कूड्, cl. 6. P. कूडति, -डितुम्, to eat; to graze; to become firm or fat or solid.
कूड्य: कूड्य कूड्य, अम्, n. a wall, = कुड्य।
कूण्: कूण् कूण्, cl. 10. P. A. कूणयति, -ते, -यितुम्, to draw together, contract, close.

कूदर: कूदर कूदर, अस्, m. the offspring of a Brāhman woman by a Ṛṣi, begotten during men-struation.

कूप्: कूप् कूप्, cl. 10. P. कूपयति, -यितुम्, to be weak, to weaken.

(said to be fr. rt. 3. कु; according to others perhaps fr. 1. कु and अप्; cf. अनूप, द्वीप), a hole, a hollow, a cave; a well; a post to which a boat or ship is moored; a mast (?); a tree or rock in the midst of a river; a leather oil vessel; (ई), f. a small well; the navel; a flask, a bottle; [cf. कूर्चल, अस्, आ, अम्, having a beard, bearded.

कूर्पास: कूर्पास कूर्पास, अस्, m. a cuirass or quilted jacket worn as armour.

कृ: कृ 1. कृ। The conjugational tenses are formed in the Veda according to four different methods, as follows: I) According to the rule for cl. 2, Pres. 2nd sing. P. कर्षि, du. कृथस्, pl. कृथ; A. कृषे; Impf. 2nd sing. P. अकर्, 3rd अकर् and अकत्; 3rd du. अकर्ताम्; pl. अकर्म, अकर्त, अक्रन्; A. अक्रि, अकृथास्, अकृत, अक्राताम्, अक्रत; Impv. Ved. चक्रुषम्); A. चक्राण; 2nd Fut. करिष्यति; Leṭ, 2nd sing. करिष्यास्; 1st Fut. कर्ता; Prec. क्रियासम्; Aor. P., Ved. चकरम्, अचक्रिरन्, अचक्रत्; A. कृषे; Class. अकार्षीत् (poet. अका-रषीत्); Pass. Aor. reflex. अकारि and अकृत; Inf. कर्तुम्; Ved. कर्तवे, कर्तवै, कर्तोस्; Ind. Part. कृत्वा, Ved. कृत्वी and कृत्वाय; to do, make, perform, accomplish, cause, effect, prepare, undertake; to do anything for the advantage or injury of another (with gen. or loc. of the person); to execute, carry out (as an order or command); to manufacture, prepare, work at, elaborate, build; to form, construct one thing out of another (with abl. or inst. of the thing); to compose, describe; to cultivate; to make a sound, utter, pronounce (often in comp. with the sounds फट्, फुट्, भाण्, वषट्, स्वधा, स्वाहा, हिम्); to employ, use; to make use of (with inst.); to accomplish any period, bring to completion, spend (e. g. वर्षाणि दश चक्रुः, they spent ten years; क्षणं कुरु, wait a mo-ment); to place, put, lay, bring, lead, to take hold of (with acc. or loc. or inst., e. g. अर्धं कृ, to win over to one's own side or party; हस्ते or पाणौ कृ, to take by the hand, to marry; हृदयेन कृ, to place in one's heart, love); to direct the thoughts, mind &c. (मनः or मतिम् or बुद्धिम् or भा-वम् &c.) towards any object, turn the attention to, resolve upon, determine on (with loc., dat., or inf. of the object, e. g. मा शोके मनः कृथाः, do not turn your mind to grief; गमनाय मतिं चक्रे, he resolved upon going; अलाबुं स्रष्टुं चक्रे, he resolved to create a gourd); to consider, turn in the mind, think; to make, to render (with two acc., e. g. आदित्यं काष्ठाम् अकुर्वत, they made the sun their goal); to procure for another, bestow, grant; A. to procure for one's self, appropriate, assume; to give aid, help any one to perform an action; to make liable; to injure, violate (e. g. कन्यां कृ, to violate a maiden); to appoint, institute; to give an order, commission; to cause to get rid of, free from (with abl.); to begin (e. g. चक्रे शोभयितुम् पुरीम्, he began to adorn the city); to proceed with, put in practice; to worship, sacrifice; (with numeral adverbs ending in धा) to divide, separate, or break up into parts, e. g. द्विधा कृ, to divide into two parts; सहस्रधा कृ, to break into a thousand pieces; (with adverbs ending in वत्) to make like or similar, to consider equivalent, e. g. राज्यं तृणवत् कृत्वा, valuing the kingdom like a straw; (with adverbs ending in सात्) to reduce anything to, cause to become, make subject, e. g. भस्मसात् कृ, to reduce to ashes; आत्मसात् कृ, to subject to one's self. The above senses of कृ may be variously modified or almost infinitely extended according to the noun with which this root is connected, as in the following exam-ples: सख्यं कृ, to contract friendship with; पूजां कृ, to honour; राज्यं कृ, to reign; स्नेहं कृ, to show affection; आज्ञां or निदेशं or शासनं or कामं or याचनां or वचः or वचनं or वाक्यं कृ, to perform any one's command or wish or request &c.; धर्मं कृ, to do one's duty; नखानि कृ, to clean one's nails; उदकं or सलिलं कृ, to offer a libation to the dead, to perform ablutions &c.; अस्त्राणि कृ, to practice the use of weapons; दर्दुरं कृ, to play on the flute; दण्डं कृ, to inflict punishment &c.; स्वरं कृ, to utter a sound; शब्दं कृ, to make a noise; कालं कृ, to bring one's time to an end, i. e. to die; चिरं कृ, to be long in doing any-thing, to delay; मनसि कृ, to take to heart, to mind, to determine, resolve upon; मनसा कृ, to place in one's mind, think of, meditate; हृदि कृ, to place in the heart, remember; वशे कृ, to place in subjection, become master of; शिरसा कृ, to place on the head; मूर्ध्ना कृ, to place on one's head, to obey, to honour: Caus. कारयति, -ते, -यि-तुम्, to cause to act or do, to cause another to perform, to have anything made or done by another (with acc. or double acc., e. g. सभां कारितवान्, he caused an assembly to be made; राज-दर्शनम् मां कारय, cause me to have an audience of the king; बानिज्यं कारयेद् वैश्यम्, he ought to cause the Vaiśya to engage in trade; or with acc. and inst., e. g. न शक्ष्यामि किञ्चित् कारयितुं त्वया, I shall not be able to have anything done by thee); to cause to manufacture or form or cultivate; to cause to place or put, to have anything placed, put upon, &c. (e. g. तं चित्र-पटं वास-गृहे भित्ताव् अकारयत्, he had the picture placed on the wall in his house). Sometimes the Caus. of कृ is used for the simple verb or without a causal significa-tion (e. g. पदं कारयति, he pronounces a word &c.; मिथ्या कारयति, he pronounces wrongly; कैकेयीम् अनु राजानं कारय, treat or deal with Kaikeyī as the king does): Desid. चिकीर्षति, -ते, to wish to make or do; to intend to do, to design, intend, begin, strive after; to wish to sacrifice or worship: Intens. चर्कर्ति, चरिकर्ति, चरीकर्ति, चर्करीति, चरिकरीति, चरीकरीति, चेक्रीयते, Ved. 3rd pl. करिक्रति, to do repeatedly; [cf. Hib. caraim, ‘I perform, execute;’ ceard, ‘an art, trade, business, function;’ sucridh, ‘easy;’ Cambro-Brit. creu, ‘to form;’ Island. gerdh, ‘action;’ Old Germ. kara-wan, ‘to prepare;’ Mod. Germ. gar, ‘prepared (as food);’ Lat. creo, cœremonia, ars (for cars); Gr. κραίνω, κρόνος.]
कृ 2. कृ, cl. 3. P., Ved. चकर्ति, अकारीत्, Intens. चर्कर्ति, to make mention of, to praise, to speak highly of (with gen.); [cf. कारु, कीरि, कीर्ति।]
कृ 3. कृ, to injure &c. See 2. कॄ।
कृत्: 1. कृत्, त्, त्, त्, making, doing, performing, accom-plishing, effecting, manufacturing, acting; one who accomplishes or performs anything, an author; often occurring at the end of compounds, see सु-कृत्, कर्म-कृत्, पाप-कृत्, &c.; (त्), m. an affix used to form nouns from roots; a noun formed with this affix. —कृद्-अन्त, अस्, m. a word ending with a Kṛt affix (such a word would be called by Pāṇini simply कृत्). —कृल्-लोप, अस्, m. the rejection of a Kṛt affix.

कृत् 2. कृत्, (for 1. कृत् see under rt. 1. कृ at p. 246), cl. 6. P. कृन्तति, चकर्त, कर्त्स्यति and कर्तिष्यति, अकर्तीत्, कर्तितुम्, to cut, cut in pieces, cut off, divide; to tear asunder, destroy: Caus. कर्तयति, to cut, divide, &c.: Desid. चिकर्तिषति and चिकृत्सति: Intens. चरीकृत्यते, चरीकर्त्ति; [cf. Lith. kertu, inf. kirsti, ‘to cut;’ Gr. κείρω, κάρσις Slav. korjû, ‘to split;’ Lat. curtus, culter; Hib. ceartaighim, ‘I prune, trim, cut;’ cuirc, ‘a knife.’]
कृत् 3. कृत्, cl. 7. P. कृणत्ति, चकर्त, कर्तिष्यति, कर्तितुम्, to twist threads, to spin; to surround, encompass; attire.
कृत: कृत, अस्, आ, अम्, done, made, accomplished, per-formed; prepared, made ready; obtained, gained, acquired; placed at hand; well done, proper, good. The preceding senses are mostly found in the Veda; the numerous other senses found in classical writers may be inferred from the meanings of the rt. कृ above. The neuter of कृत is used with सह or with the inst. alone in the sense of ‘done with,’ ‘away with,’ ‘enough of,’ ‘no need of,’ &c. (e. g. कृतं सन्देहेन, away with doubt; कृतम् परिहासेन, enough of joking). कृत is often found at the end of a compound, e. g. पूर्व-कृत, done formerly; जन्मान्तर-कृत, done in a former state of existence; (अस्), m., N. of one of the Viśva-devās; of a son of Vasu-deva; of a son of Sannati and pupil of Hiraṇya-nābha; of a son of Kṛta-ratha and father of Vibudha; of a son of Jaya and father of Haryavana; of a son of Cyavana and father of Upari-cara; (अम्), n. deed, work, action; service done, kind action, benefit; consequence, result; aim, object, design; stake at a game; prize or booty gained in battle; N. of the die or of the side of a die marked with four points; (according to some) the collective name of the four dice in opposition to the fifth die, called कलि; N. of the first of the four ages of the world (also called सत्य or ‘the golden age’) comprehending together with the morning and even-ing dawn 4,800 years of men, according to the Mahā-bhārata; but according to the Purāṇas 4,800 years of the gods, or 1,728000 years of men. —कृत-कपट, अस्, आ, अम्, deceiving, beguiling, fraudulent. —कृत-कर्तव्य, अस्, आ, अम्, one who has performed what was to be done, who has done his duty; having done or discharged one's duty. —कृत-कर्मन्, आ, आ, अ, one who has done his work or duty; skilful, clever, able. —कृत-कल्प, अस्, आ, अम्, one who knows the customary rites. —कृत-काम, अस्, आ, अम्, one whose desire is attained or fulfilled. —कृत-कार्य, अम्, n. an attained object; (अस्, आ, अम्), one who has done his work or obtained his object; one who has no need of another person's aid (with inst.). —कृत-काल, अस्, m. appointed time; (अस्, आ, अम्), fixed, settled as to time; sent, deposited &c. for a certain time; one who has accomplished a certain time, who has waited a certain time. —कृत-कूर्च्छक, अस्, आ, अम्, tied up as a small bundle or brush. —कृत-कृत्य, अम्, n. what has been done and what is to be done; an attained object; (अस्, आ, अम्), having successfully accomplished a business; one who has accomplished or attained any object or purpose; contented, satis-fied; clever. —कृतकृत्य-ता, f. or कृतकृत्य-त्व, अम्, n. the full discharge of any duty or realisa-tion of any object, accomplishment, attainment, success. —कृत-कोटि, इस्, m., N. of a Kāśyapa; an epithet of Upavarṣa. —कृत-कोप, अस्, आ, अम्, angry, indignant. —कृत-कौतुक, अस्, ई, अम्, playful. —कृत-क्रय, अस्, m. a purchaser, a buyer. —कृत-क्रिय, अस्, आ, अम्, one who has finished or accomplished any object in which he is engaged; one who has attained his end or object; one who has fulfilled his duty or performed a religious cere-mony. —कृत-क्रुध, अस्, आ, अम्, angry, resentful. —कृत-क्षण, अस्, आ, अम्, one who is waiting for the exact moment, one who waits impatiently for a person or thing, (with प्रति or with the inf. or at the end of a comp., e. g. कृत-क्षणाहं ते गमनम् प्रति, I am waiting impatiently for thy going; ते भूमिं गन्तुं कृत-क्षनाः, they are waiting for the time to proceed to the earth); (अस्), m., N. of a prince. —कृत-घात-यत्न, अस्, आ, अम्, making efforts to slay, one who tries to kill. —कृत-घ्न, अस्, ई, अम्, destroying past trans-actions or (benefits) done, unmindful of (services) rendered, recompensing evil for good, not acknow-ledging good offices or benefits received, ungrateful; defeating or rendering vain all previous measures. —कृतघ्न-ता, f. or कृतघ्न-त्व, अम्, n. in-gratitude. —कृत-चूड, अस्, m. a boy on whom the ceremony of tonsure has been performed. —कृत-चेतस्, आस्, m., N. of a Brāhman. —कृत-च्छिद्रा, f. the plant Luffa Acutangula. —कृत-जन्मन्, आ, आ, अ, born, produced, generated. —कृत-ज्ञ, अस्, आ, अम्, remembering past transactions, mindful of former aid or favours, grateful; observing propriety, correct in conduct; (अस्), m. a dog; an epithet of Śiva. —कृतज्ञ-ता, f. or कृतज्ञ-त्व, अम्, n. gratitude. —कृतञ्-जय, अस्, m., N. of the seventeenth Vyāsa; also of a prince. —कृत-तनुत्राण, अस्, आ, अम्, mailed, having covered one's self with armour. —कृत-तीर्थ, अस्, m. one who has visited holy places &c., one who frequents them; a guide; an adviser, one fertile in expedients. —कृत-त्रा, f., N. of a plant, = त्रायमाणा. —कृत-त्व, अम्, n. the state of being done or effected. —कृत-दार, अस्, आ, अम्, married; [cf. दारक्रिया।] —कृत-दास, अस्, m. one who offers himself as a servant for a certain time, a self-engaged servant, a hired servant. —कृत-द्युति, इस्, f., N. of the wife of king Citraketu. —कृत-द्विष्ट, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. angry with the doings of another person. —कृत-धन्वन्, आ, m., N. of a son of Kanaka. —कृत-धी, ईस्, ईस्, इ, prudent, considerate; learned, educated. —कृत-ध्वंस, अस्, आ, अम्, defeated, overpowered; injured, destroyed; destroying past transactions; [cf. कृत-घ्न।] —कृत-ध्वज, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. furnished with banners; (अस्), m., N. of a prince, a son of Dharma-dhvaja. —कृत-ध्वस्त, अस्, आ, अम्, lost after being once possessed or acquired. —कृत-नख, अस्, आ, अम्, one who has cleaned his nails. —कृत-नाशक, अस्, ई, अम्, ungrateful; [cf. कृत-घ्न।] —कृत-नित्यक्रिय, अस्, आ, अम्, having duly attended to the daily religious observances. —कृत-निर्णेजन, अस्, m. a penitent, one who has per-formed penance or made expiation. —कृत-निश्चय, अस्, आ, अम्, one who has made a resolution, resolved, determined; confident, sure, certain. —कृत-पर्व, अम्, n. (?) the golden age of the world. —कृत-पश्चात्ताप, अस्, आ, अम्, showing regret or penitence. —कृत-पुङ्ख, अस्, आ, अम्, ‘one who has fixed the feathers of his arrows,’ skilled in archery. —कृत-पुण्य, अस्, आ, अम्, accomplished in virtuous acts. —कृत-पूर्व, अस्, आ, अम्, done formerly. —कृत-पूर्व-नाशन, अम्, n. forgetting past services, in-gratitude; [cf. कृत-घ्न।] —कृत-पूर्विन्, ई, इणी, इ, one by whom anything was formerly done. —कृत-पौरुष, अस्, आ, अम्, behaving gallantly. —कृत-प्रणाम, अस्, आ, अम्, making obeisance, saluting. —कृत-प्रतिकृत, अम्, n. assault and counter-assault; attack and resistance; retaliation for an assault. —कृत-प्रतिज्ञ, अस्, आ, अम्, ful-filling a promise or agreement. —कृत-प्रयत्न, अस्, आ, अम्, making effort, active, industrious, per-severing. —कृत-फल, अस्, आ, अम्, successful, fruitful; (अम्), n. result, consequence of an act; a poisonous substance; (आ), f., N. of a plant; [cf. कोल-शिम्बी।] —कृत-बन्धु, उस्, m., N. of a prince. —कृत-बाहु, उस्, उस्, उ, laying hands upon, touch-ing. —कृत-बुद्धि, इस्, इस्, इ, one who has made a resolution, a man of resolute or firm character; resolved; informed of one's duty, one who knows how religious rites ought to be conducted; learned, wise. —कृत-ब्रह्मन्, आ, आ, अ, Ved. one who has performed his devotions; (a deity) towards whom devotion is made, (a sacrifice) in which prayers are duly offered. —कृत-भय, अस्, आ, अम्, alarmed, apprehensive. —कृत-भाव, अस्, आ, अम्, one whose mind is directed towards anything, determined, re-solved. —कृत-भूत-मैत्र, अस्, ई, अम्, friendly to all. —कृत-भोजन, अस्, आ, अम्, one who has dined or made a meal. —कृत-मङ्गल, अस्, आ, अम्, blessed, consecrated. —कृत-मति, इस्, इस्, इ, one who has taken a resolution, one who has resolved upon anything. —कृत-मन्दार, अस्, m., N. of a man. —कृत-मन्यु, उस्, उस्, उ, angry, offended, indignant. —कृत-मार्ग, अस्, आ, अम्, having a road or path made; In the earlier language कृत्वस् is used as a separate word, but native grammarians regard it only as an affix, and it is so used in classical Sanskrit; it was perhaps originally an acc. plur. fr. a noun कृतु, formed by the affix तु fr. the root 1. कृ; [cf. also कृत् in सकृत्।]

कृप: कृप, अस्, m., N. of a man described in the Veda as a friend of Indra; (अस्), m. and (ई), f., N. of the son and daughter of the sage Śaradvat, (he performed severe penance and thereby alarmed the jealous Indra, who sent a nymph to tempt him, but without success; however, twin sons were born to the sage in a clump of grass (शर-स्तम्बे), who were found by king Śāntanu and out of pity (कृपा) taken home and reared as his own; the daughter, Kṛpī, married Droṇa, and had by him a son called Aśvatthāman; the son, Kṛpa, became one of the privy council at Hastināpur, and is sometimes called Gautama, some-times Śāradvata. कृष्ण: कृष्ण 1. कृष्ण, अस्, आ, अम् (said to be fr. rt. कृष्), black, dark, dark-blue (opposed to श्वेत, शुक्ल, रोहित, and अरुण); wicked, evil; (अस्), m. black, the colour, or dark-blue, which is often con-founded with black by the Hindūs; the black ante-lope; a kind of beast of prey (described in the Veda as feeding on carrion and dead corpses); a crow; the Indian cuckoo or Kokila; the plant Carissa Carandas; the dark half of the lunar month from full to new moon [cf. कृष्ण-पक्ष below]; the fourth or Kali-yuga; N. of one of the poets of the Ṛg-veda descended from Aṅgiras; N. of a celebrated Avatār of the god Viṣṇu, or sometimes identified with Viṣṇu himself, as distinct from his ten Avatārs or incarnations. (In the earlier legends he ap-pears as a great hero and teacher; in the more recent he is deified, and is often represented as a young and amorous shepherd with flowing hair and a flute in his hand. The following are a few particulars of his birth and history as related in the Purāṇas &c.: Vasu-deva, who was a descendant of Yadu and Yayāti, had two wives, Rohiṇī and Devakī. The latter had eight sons, of whom the eighth was Kṛṣṇa. Kaṃsa, king of Mathurā and cousin of Devakī, was informed by a prediction that one of these sons would kill him. He therefore kept Vasu-deva and his wife in confinement, and slew their first six children. The seventh was Bala-rāma, who was saved by being abstracted from the womb of Devakī and transferred to that of Rohiṇī. The eighth was Kṛṣṇa, who was born with black skin and a peculiar mark on his breast. His father Vasu-deva managed to escape from Mathurā with the child, and favoured by the gods found a herdsman named Nanda, whose wife Yaśodā had just been delivered of a son, which Vasu-deva conveyed to Devakī, after substituting his own in its place. Nanda with his wife Yaśodā took the infant Kṛṣṇa and settled first in Gokula or Vraja, and afterwards in Vṛndāvana, where Kṛṣṇa and Bala-rāma grew up together, roaming in the woods and joining in the sports of the herdsmen's sons. Kṛṣṇa as a youth contested the sovereignty of Indra, and was victorious over that god, who descended from heaven to praise Kṛṣṇa, and made him lord over the cattle. Kṛṣṇa is described as sporting constantly with the Gopīs or shepherdesses, of whom a thousand became his wives, though only eight are specified, Rādhā being the favourite. Kṛṣṇa built and fortified a city called Dvāraka in Gujarāt, and thither transported the inhabitants of Mathurā after killing Kaṃsa. Kṛṣṇa had various wives be-sides the Gopīs, and by Rukmiṇī had a son Pra-dyumna, who is usually identified with Kāma-deva; with Jainas, Kṛṣṇa is one of the nine black Vasu-devas; with Buddhists he is the chief of the black demons, who are the enemies of Buddha and the white demons); N. of a king of the Nāgas; N. of an Asura or demon; N. of Arjuna, the most renowned of the Pāṇḍu princes (so named apparently from his colour as a child, see Mahā-bh. Virāṭa-parva 1389; the dual कृष्णौ = Kṛṣṇa and Arjuna); N. of Vyāsa; of Kṛṣṇa Hārīta; of a son of Śuka by Pīvarī, a teacher of the Yoga; N. of a pupil of Bharadvāja; of Dāśārha; of a son of Havirdhāna;
